name: Aanchal Khandelwal
bio: Aanchal Khandelwal is a Senior Software Engineer at Adobe who brings 7+ years of software engineering experience to complex platform problems. She began her career building high-throughput backend systems and data pipelines, which shaped her practical approach to infrastructure costs at scale. Today she works on Adobe's internal multi-tenant Kubernetes platform, tackling infrastructure optimization and operational challenges across hundreds of clusters.

name: Aaron Campbell
bio: Aaron Campbell has spent 25+ years in security, from his early days as an OpenBSD developer and vulnerability researcher to DDoS mitigation, traffic engineering, identity, and access control. He now focuses on network defense and cloud infrastructure at Isovalent, part of Cisco.

name: Abby Bangser
bio:
Abby is a Principal Engineer at Syntasso delivering Kratix, the open-source cloud-native framework for providing the execution later for your internal platforms. Her keen interest in supporting internal development comes from over a decade of experience in consulting and product delivery roles across platform, site reliability, and quality engineering.

Abby is a CNCF Ambassador, Team Topologies Advocate, emeritus CNCF Platforms Working Group lead, and co-host of the #CoffeeOps London meetup.

name: Abdel Sghiouar
bio: Abdel Sghiouar is a senior Cloud Developer Advocate @Google Cloud. A co-host of the Kubernetes Podcast by Google and a CNCF Ambassador. His focused areas are GKE/Kubernetes, Service Mesh and Serverless. Abdel started his career in datacenters and infrastructure in Morocco where he is originally.

name: Abhilash Somasamudramath
bio: Abhilash leads product management for Robotics Infrastructure at NVIDIA, building the simulation, data, and agentic platforms that get robots out of the lab and into the world.
tagline: Product Lead for Robotics Infrastructure, NVIDIA

name: Adam Buran
bio: Adam Buran is a Principal Software Engineer focused on AI infrastructure, Kubernetes, and large-scale distributed systems. He builds cloud-native platforms that enable machine learning workloads, GPU scheduling, and reliable production infrastructure. His work spans platform engineering, developer tooling, and scalable data systems, with a focus on simplifying complex distributed architectures.

name: Adam Wolfe Gordon
bio: Adam Wolfe Gordon is a principal engineer at Upbound, focused on Crossplane and developer tooling for platform engineers. He previously worked on Kubernetes, among other things, at DigitalOcean, and as a platform engineer at Docker. Adam is interested in infrastructure products and developer tools, and likes to spend as much time thinking about what we build as how we build it. Outside of work Adam enjoys ski racing, bikes, and not being near computers very much.

name: Adam Gordon Bell
bio: Adam Gordon Bell is a Community Engineer at Pulumi and creator of the CoRecursive podcast, where he's interviewed the creators of SQLite, Chef, and PowerShell (100+ episodes). He spent two decades building developer tools, including container security at Tenable and container-native build pipelines at Earthly. He spoke at SCaLE 20x on container runtimes, SCaLE 23x on AI agents in production, and PyTexas on building a personal AI coach, with an upcoming talk at MLCon San Diego.

name: Aditya Sirish A Yelgundhalli
bio: Aditya is a software engineer at Bloomberg where he works on software supply chain security. He is a maintainer of a number of supply chain security efforts like in-toto, SLSA, and gittuf, in addition to contributing to other systems like TUF and Sigstore. Reach out to chat about software supply chain security, open source software, in-toto, TUF, gittuf, and just about anything else!
tagline: Software supply chain security researcher and engineer

name: Adrian Mouat
bio:
Adrian has been involved with containers from the early days of Docker and authored the O’Reilly book “Using Docker”. 

He works at Chainguard  whose mission is to make the software lifecycle secure by default. His current focus is on improving the standard of security and provenance guarantees in container images.

name: Adrian Ng
bio: Adrian Ng has spent two decades building enterprise-grade infrastructure. As an Engineering Director at Verkada, he leads the platform infrastructure teams keeping Verkada's cloud reliable across more than 2 million devices globally. He previously led engineering teams building products from scratch at Google Cloud and Oracle. Adrian holds a BS and MS degree from Carnegie Mellon University.

name: Aidan Carson
bio: Aidan Carson is a software engineer at GEICO, where he leads the hybrid cloud fabric team in creating GEICO's next generation of infrastructure. Responsible for the core logic of the management plane powering this infrastructure, he brings insights from the trials and tribulations of transforming into modern zero-trust infrastructure based on Istio and SPIRE in the real world. Aidan brings experience from nearly a decade working on proxy and service mesh infrastructure at Solo.io and NGINX.

name: Ajay Vohra
bio: Ajay Vohra is a Generative AI Applied engineer, with special interest in application of vision transformers in autonomous driving. Prior to joining Amazon, Ajay worked in the area of massively parallel grid-computing for financial risk modeling.
tagline: AWS, Principal Generative AI Applied Engineer

name: Ajmal Ali kannu
bio:
Ajmal Ali kannu is a Senior Full Stack Engineer focused on building resilient, high-scale systems in the financial domain. He has worked extensively with open source technologies to design and deliver cloud-native apps handling high-throughput transactional workloads.
 
Ajmal is passionate about sharing practical lessons from production—especially the things that don’t go as planned—and helping teams build systems that scale and survive in real-world conditions.

name: Akhil Mohan
bio: Akhil works as a Software Engineer at Broadcom. An active contributor to projects in cloud native and container ecosystem. Akhil is a reviewer for containerd and a maintainer of kubernetes publishing-bot. He works mostly on container runtimes and kubernetes sig-node aspects.

name: Akihiro Suda
bio: Akihiro Suda is a software engineer at NTT Corporation. He has been a maintainer of Moby (dockerd), BuildKit, containerd, runc, etc. He is also a founder of nerdctl and Lima (CNCF project).

name: Alay Patel
bio: Alay is a Senior Software Engineer at Nvidia where he works on cloud gaming service, managing infrastructure for GPU workloads. He is passionate about open source with a focus on Kubernetes and platform engineering.

name: Aleksander Slominski
bio: Aleksander Slominski is a Research Staff Member in the Hybrid Cloud Programming Models and Systems department at the IBM T.J. Watson Research Center.  He works on bringing serverless experience to running HPC and AI workloads in Kubernetes, participate in open source LLM-D project  He organizes International Workshops on Serverless Computing (WoSC) to bring together researchers and industry practitioners to discuss their experiences and thoughts on future directions.

name: Alessandro Cannarella
bio: Alessandro Cannarella is a Senior Software Engineer at vCluster Labs, with expertise in cloud infrastructure and cloud-native runtimes. He is a Core maintainer of the CNCF project Falco, actively contributing to the broader cloud-native ecosystem, driving innovation within the open-source space. Before joining vCluster Labs, he was an Open Source Engineer at Sysdig and previously worked as a Platform Engineer and Cloud Engineer. Outside of work, he enjoys sports and Formula 1.

name: Alessandro Fael Garcia
bio: Alessandro is a Community Evangelist / Sr Solutions Engineer in the F5 community team, where he empowers users in their journey to stay ahead of the curve by using the latest F5 / NGINX tech offerings. Alessandro is also the primary maintainer of the NGINX community forum, and implementer of community best practices efforts on the various F5 GitHub OSS orgs. In his free time, Alessandro enjoys theatre, cinema, traveling, and any and all types of exercise.
tagline: Community Evangelist / Sr Solutions Engineer (F5 Community)

name: Alex Chircop
bio: Principal Engineer at Google. Member of the CNCF Technical Oversight Committee. Previously Chief Architect at Akamai, a founder and CTO of Ondat (formerly StorageOS), building software defined solutions for cloud native environments, and a co-chair of the CNCF Storage TAG. Before embarking on the startup adventure he spent over 25 years engineering infrastructure platforms for companies like Nomura and Goldman Sachs.

name: Alex Yuskauskas
bio: Alex Yuskauskas is a Senior System Software Engineer at NVIDIA, NodeWright project lead, and is actively working on improving the OS lifecycle of NVIDIA’s kubernetes clusters using Nodewright.
tagline: Senior Systems Software Engineer at NVIDIA

name: Alexa Griffith
bio:
Alexa Griffith is a Senior Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat, working as a Forward Deployed Engineer on production AI systems at scale. Previously, she spent 4.5 years at Bloomberg on the AI Inference Platform team.

She contributes to KServe, Envoy AI Gateway, and llm-d, serves as a TAG Infrastructure Tech Lead, and has presented across multiple KubeCons and served on various CNCF committees.

Alexa also hosts Alexa's Input, a podcast featuring engineers and open-source leaders.
tagline: Senior Principal Software Engineer, CNCF TAG Infra Tech Lead

name: Alexander Kanevskiy
bio: Alexander is currently employed by Intel as Principal Engineer, Cloud Software, focusing on various aspects in Kubernetes: Resource and Device Management for CPU, Memory and accelerators, Cluster Lifecycle. Alexander has over 25+ years of experience in areas of Linux distributions, SCM, Networking, Infrastructure, Release Engineering, Cloud Orchestration, Continuous Integration & Delivery. Alexander is an active member of Kubernetes SIG-Node and CNCF TAG Workloads Foundation.
tagline: Intel, Principal Engineer, Cloud Orchestration Software

name: Alexander Meijer
bio: Alex is an OpenCost maintainer and works in cost observability and optimization at IBM Kubecost. He lives in New Hampshire and enjoys hiking and time with family.

name: Alexander Perlman
bio: Alexander Perlman is a Distinguished Engineer at Capital One's Machine Learning Experience organization. His areas of focus include distributed compute and workflow orchestration. He lives in the NYC metro area (aka NJ and ashamed) with his wife and four young children. He believes that the correct pronunciation of "kubectl" is "kube-control," not "kube-cuddle."

name: Alexandre Gaudreault
bio: Alexandre is a Software Developer at Intuit working on the core Argo team. He is a maintainer of the CNCF-graduated project Argo CD. He thrives on building internal developer platforms using open-source technologies to increase development velocity. Outside of work, you may find him backpacking around the world, always seeking his next adventure.
tagline: Staff Software Developer & Argo Maintainer @ Intuit

name: Alexis Ngoga
bio: Alexis Ngoga is an AI Engineer and Solutions Architect (MS, Engineering Artificial Intelligence, Carnegie Mellon University). At RwandAir he bridges modern AI/data workflows with legacy enterprise systems. His work spans AI agents, MLOps/LLMOps, and protocol-based integrations (MCP, A2A, WSDL), focused on safe, incremental adoption of AI in production. He builds operators and platform tooling that make AI-driven decisions explainable to the humans responsible for them.
tagline: AI/ML | Agentic AI Systems| Solution Architect

name: Ali Aqel
bio:
Ali is a Software Engineer at Stripe, operating Kubernetes as part of Stripe's Payment Processing platform. At Stripe, he has focused on onboarding applications to Pod Autoscaling and his work here has produced contributions to the Kubernetes Event Driven Autoscaling (KEDA) project.

Outside of work, Ali enjoys running, skiing, biking, and playing the role of can opener to his four cats.

name: Alolita Sharma
bio: Alolita Sharma is a OpenTelemetry maintainer and GC member. Also she is a CNCF End-User TAB & GB member. She leads Apple’s AIML observability teams. She contributes to open source, open standards at OpenTelemetry, Unicode, W3C. She has been co-chair of CNCF's Observability TAG and has served on the boards of the OSI, SFLC.in and Unicode Consortium. Previously Alolita led observability and search engineering teams at AWS and has managed engineering teams at IBM, PayPal, Twitter, Wikipedia.
tagline: OpenTelemetry GC, CNCF End-User TAB and GB Member, Platform Engineering, Observability at Apple
role: Observability Engineering Leader at Apple, OpenTelemetry Governance Committee Member

name: Alvaro Aleman
bio: Alvaro is a software engineer with a deep passion for infrastructure and open source

name: Alyssa Goins
bio: Alyssa Goins is a Software Engineer at Red Hat and a regular contributor to the Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) project. Since joining the Kubeflow community in March 2025, she has contributed to the development of several features including the KFP MLflow plugin.

name: Aman Singh
bio:
Principal Software Engineer in the office of Microsoft Azure's CTO and maintainer of Drasi. Organizer of the CNCF community group for Seattle.

Speaker @ KubeCon NA 2025 and program committee member for KubeCon India 2026 and KubeCon Japan 2026, Aman also mentors students through GSoC and LFX on projects spanning agentic AI, MCP & IoT.

Aman has 12+ years of distributed systems experience at LinkedIn and Microsoft - spanning stream processing, and building new Azure services from the ground up.
tagline: Engineering Leader at Microsoft Azure CTO's Office · Drasi Maintainer · CNCF organizer

name: Amy Chen
bio: Amy Chen is a software engineer at CoreWeave. Today, she helps build a platform that enables CoreWeave's fleet of AIML workloads. With her entire professional career built on top of Kubernetes, Amy has previously worked at Apple, VMware, Heptio, and Rancher Labs.

name: AmyJune Hineline
bio: AmyJune currently works with the Linux Foundation as their Global Skills Community Architect. She is responsible for supporting the Certification team’s efforts in building and maintaining exams and related documentation for exam products in the Linux Foundation’s certification portfolio.

name: Ana Biazetti
bio: Ana is a senior architect at Red Hat Openshift AI product organization, focusing on Model Customization, Fine Tuning and Distributed Training. Previously she created Financial AI solutions, working with major clients to architect and develop Gen AI enterprise solutions at IBM. Ana is an experienced speaker and has presented at several events, including TechXchange, Women in Payments, SIBOS, Think and SWE.
tagline: Senior Principal Software Engineer, RedHat AI

name: Anca Sailer
bio: Dr. Anca Sailer is an IBM Distinguished Engineer at the T. J. Watson Research Lab where she transforms the clients compliance processes into an engineering practice. Dr. Sailer received her Ph.D. in CS from Sorbonne Universités, France and joined IBM Research in 2003. Dr. Sailer has over 100 patents, co-authored in IEEE & ACM journals and conferences, and co-edited 3 books. She actively contributes to the CNCF TAG Security and Compliance driving innovation and collaboration within the community.

name: Andjelko Iharos
bio: Andjelko is the VP of Architecture at HAProxy Technologies. He is responsible for designing and overseeing the implementation of solutions and services at all scales—from low-level, microsecond-optimized software to massive automated clusters processing tens of billions of requests per day. Andjelko works with tools such as Python, C, Golang and many more.

name: André Wanlin
bio: André, a full Stack Developer from Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada, is a Core Maintainer, Community Plugin Maintainer and Documentation Maintainer of the Backstage open source project having contributed 3 plugins as well as various features, bug fixes and documentation updates. He's also an active CNCF Ambassador and co-chairs BackstageCon. When he's offline you can catch him at the local dog park with his Frenchton Bailey!

name: Andrew Block
bio: Andrew Block is a Distinguished Architect at Red Hat who works with organizations to adopt Open Source solutions with a focus on Cloud Native, security and emerging technologies. Andrew is the author of multiple technical publications and frequently shares his knowledge and experiences related to relevant industry topics. He is a recognized leader, maintainer and contributor within the Open Source community, and partners with organizations to help employ Open Source practices and their benefits.

name: Andrew Burden
bio:
I am a community facilitator for the KubeVirt project (kubevirt.io and https://www.github.com/kubevirt/community)

In a past life I worked on documentation and customer projects in the virtualization and then container space. Away from work, I am a father of a small human, and do a lot less adventuring than I used to. But I still love all things bikes, trails, playing music, cooking ambitious recipes, and self-hosting.

name: Andrew Collins
bio: Andrew is a Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat, focused on scaling and monitoring Kubernetes-based platforms.

name: Andrew Hendrickson
bio: I serve as Chief of the FCC’s Office of Engineering and Technology, guiding spectrum policy, equipment authorization, and technical strategy. I previously led technology efforts in the Enforcement Bureau across cybersecurity, privacy, and critical infrastructure. Before the FCC, I spent two decades in telecom, including 5G work at Verizon. My background spans cloud, networking, cybersecurity, and GIS.
tagline: Chief, Office of Engineering & Technology at Federal Communications Commission

name: Andrew Martin
bio: Andrew has an incisive security engineering ethos gained building and destroying high-traffic web applications. Proficient in systems development, testing, and operations, he is at his happiest profiling and securing every tier of a cloud native system, and has battle-hardened experience delivering containerised solutions to enterprise and government. He is CEO at https://control-plane.io

name: Andrew McNamara
bio: Andrew McNamara is passionate about usable CI/CD, security, and DevSecOps, drawing from his experience of building and shipping containerized software at IBM and Red Hat. As a SLSA maintainer, Andrew is helping people identify how to approach and understand supply chain security. He works at Red Hat as a contributor to the Konflux CI project, providing developer flexibility without sacrificing software security.

name: Andrew Thorp
bio: Open Source Software Developer and Maintainer. Currently working at Red Hat as a Senior Software Engineer on OpenShift Pipelines (TektonCD upstream). Passionate about developer tooling and owning one's tools. Human.
tagline: Red Hat, Senior Software Engineer - Openshift Pipelines, TektonCD Maintainer

name: Andrew Sy Kim
bio: Andrew Sy Kim is a Staff Software Engineer at Google working on Ray, KubeRay and GKE.

name: Andrey Velichkevich
bio: Andrey Velichkevich is an AI Engineer at Apple and a key contributor to the Kubeflow and Kubernetes projects. He serves on the Kubeflow Steering Committee and is a co-chair for Kubernetes WG WAS and Checkpoint/Restore. In addition, Andrey is an active member of the Batch WG, SIG Scheduling, and the CNCF AI TSG. He is a co-author of the CNCF AI White Paper and actively contributes to multiple AI initiatives that advance the CNCF community and the broader cloud-native AI ecosystem.

name: Andy Anderson
bio:
Andy is an experienced software architect with a strong track record of leading research and engineering teams on hybrid cloud and Kubernetes-based platform development. He has a wealth of experience in software development, cloud computing, and data analysis.

Andy is particularly adept at combining continuous integration and delivery practices, containerization and orchestration technologies, and cloud computing products and services for use with platform engineering efforts.

name: Andy Suderman
bio: Andy Suderman is CTO at Fairwinds, a managed Kubernetes-as-a-Service provider. Andy has worked with cloud native technologies for the last ten years helping organizations adopt and manage Kubernetes. Andy is the creator and primary developer of Goldilocks, an open source tool that helps companies leverage the VPA in Kubernetes. He has presented on many CNCF Cloud Native Live virtual events, Containers from the Couch and is a co-chair of the Policy Working Group, as well as a CNCF Ambassador.

name: Aniket Shaha
bio: Backend and AI Infrastructure Engineer

name: Anish Ramasekar
bio: Anish Ramasekar is a software engineer at Microsoft, where he works on the Azure Container Upstream team building features for Kubernetes upstream and various CNCF projects that power Azure Kubernetes Service. He is a co-chair of Kubernetes SIG Auth and a maintainer of the Secrets Store CSI Driver project.

name: Ankit Goyal
bio: Ankit Goyal is a Principal Engineer on the LinkedIn AI Platform team, where he focuses on the Agentic platform and leads core GPU efficiency efforts for the model training platform. A veteran of LinkedIn's infrastructure evolution, Ankit also spearheaded the transition to containerization, built the company's Kubernetes-based AI platform, and designed frameworks for ML pipelines and datacenter hardware orchestration.
tagline: LinkedIn, AI Platform, Principal Staff Software Engineer

name: Ann Wallace
bio: Ann Wallace is the Chief Adventure Officer at Girls Gone Wildwood, where she can be found seeking type 2 fun adventures in the PNW. Before becoming a full time dirtbag with her dog Cedar, she held leadership and architecture roles in security and cloud at Edera, Okta, Shopify, Google, and Nike. Ann speaks regularly at conferences on topics like compliance, container security, and using storytelling to make security education actually stick.

name: Anne Lau
bio: Anne Lau is a Senior Software Engineer at Salesforce, working on the Kubernetes infrastructure at Salesforce. Her recent work focuses on closing the developer-experience gap between single-cluster kubectl and the multi-cluster infrastructure underneath. Anne contributes to Open Cluster Management (OCM), a CNCF sandbox project, and is a first-time KubeCon speaker.
tagline: Senior Software Engineer, Salesforce — Hyperforce Kubernetes Platform

name: Ant(on) Weiss
bio: 25 years in tech, marketing and leadership roles. All about software delivery optimization. 5 years in technical and executive training.  Expert in Leadership, DevOps, Lean, Systems Thinking, Continuous Delivery, Cloud Native and Agentic Systems. Coder, speaker, writer. Fixated on improving the ways humans (and agents) collaborate by telling mind-provoking stories.

name: Antoine Roy
bio: I am a software engineer at Mistral AI, working on Mistral Compute, the company's sovereign GPU cloud. After ten years building in cloud native environments, I am now in the bare-metal world, trying to recreate the simplicity of the cloud on top of physical racks.
tagline: Lead Software Engineer, Compute Infrastructure at Mistral AI

name: Anton Alexander
bio: Anton Alexander is a Platform Engineer focused on developer experience. He works on Kubernetes offerings running on public and private clouds that power business-critical software at scale, with an emphasis on making infrastructure easier for engineering teams to use, adopt, and trust. Lately he has been building AI-driven tools to simplify troubleshooting and help teams interact with complex systems more naturally.

name: Antonio Jimenez Martinez
bio:
I am a Tech Lead Software Engineer at Cisco ThousandEyes, specializing in observability to ensure our customers can effectively monitor their products. My recent work involves using OpenTelemetry to stream telemetry data, enhancing network visibility and performance for our clients.


I actively participate in the tech community, frequently attending conferences and meet-ups to share knowledge and stay abreast of industry trends.
tagline: Cisco ThousandEyes, Tech Lead Software Engineer

name: Antonio Ojea
bio: Antonio Ojea is a Software Engineer at Google, where he works on Kubernetes. He is one of the top contributors of the Kubernetes project, Tech Lead in Kubernetes SIG Network & Testing with a proven track record in leading technical initiatives to enhance Kubernetes networking stability and performance. Enthusiastic advocate for strong testing practices within open-source communities.
tagline: Senior Staff Software Engineer at Google

name: Anubhav Dhoot
bio: Anubhav Dhoot is Senior Vice President of Engineering at Salesforce, where he owns compute and runtime platforms, driving its multi-substrate, cloud-native infrastructure. With 20+ years in distributed systems (ex-Cloudera, Microsoft, Apache Hadoop committer), he oversees Kubernetes, service mesh, and fleet operations across thousands of clusters to elevate system reliability, cost efficiency, and developer velocity.

name: Aramis Sennyey
bio: For his day job, Aramis works on a TS monorepo for DoorDash, focusing mainly on CI/CD and developer experience around web technologies. He's also a maintainer for the OpenAPI tooling and documentation project areas for Backstage.
role: Core Maintainer of Backstage, Software Engineer

name: Arka Saha
bio: Arka Saha, a Broadcom Software Engineer, leads Kubernetes releases & maintenance for VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF). He manages Broadcom's Prow infrastructure, ensuring long-term support for k8s, etcd, containers, Golang & related components. Previously, he managed Red Hat OpenShift clusters & developed Golang operators for Tekton at IBM CIO. He has been contributing to k8s and etcd since early last year and actively supports the community by improving pipelines by contributing to test-infra.
tagline: Software Engineer at Broadcom, Kubernetes Contributor

name: Arndt Schwenkschuster
bio: Arndt is a Software Engineer focused on Workload Identity. He's a SPIFFE maintainer and member of the SPIFFE Steering Committee. He also contributes actively in the IETF OAuth and WIMSE working groups and has authored multiple adopted documents.

name: Arpit Agrawal
bio: I am an active Kubernetes contributor. I recently authored a SIG Spotlight Blog on SIG CLI, provided valuable support during community elections (Writing emails and Tweets), currently shadowed under the social media coordinator of SIG_Contibex-comms, and made contributions to improve documentation.

name: Arthur Vardevanyan
bio: Arthur is a K8s Platform Engineering Lead at Ford Motor Company out of the Ford College Graduate Rotational Program, and focuses on all things Kubernetes, Infrastructure, and Cloud Computing. Arthur attended Lawrence Technological University and holds a Masters in Computer Science.

name: Artur Beznosyuk
bio: Software engineer working on infrastructure and backend systems

name: Artur Wierzbicki
bio: Artur is a software engineer at heart and an engineering manager at Grafana, where he works in the AI Department which maintains Grafana Assistant, Grafana CLI, AI Observability, o11y-bench and many other products. He also leads a software engineering leadership community in the UAE and can usually be found daydreaming about his next Himalayan climb.
tagline: Senior Engineering Manager at Grafana Labs

name: Arunesh Pandey
bio: I am a software engineer with a focus towards systems engineering.  Most recently, I have been working as a tech lead on VM Service -- modernizing the platform to enable Kubernetes style deployment and management of VMs alongside pods and Kubernetes clusters.

name: Arunkumar Amaran
bio: Senior Software Engineering Leader with over 19 years of industry experience leading large-scale technology and data transformation initiatives, primarily within complex retail and enterprise environments. My expertise includes cloud-native architecture and implementation, generative AI and conversational agent platforms, enterprise data engineering, business process automation, and modern software development practices.
tagline: Macys, Tech Manager, Data Engineering and Architecture

name: Aseef Imran
bio: Aseef is a Software Engineer at Red Hat, where he works on KubeVirt. He is an active upstream contributor to the project. Aseef holds a Bachelor's and Master's degree in Computer Science from Boston University.

name: Ashok Chandrasekar
bio: Ashok Chandrasekar is a Staff Software Engineer at Google working on AI Inference performance evaluation and optimization for Google Kubernetes Engine. He is a project lead and maintainer of Inference Perf and co-lead of SIG Benchmarking in llm-d. Previously, he was a Staff Engineer at VMware where he led the cluster lifecycle management area for Tanzu Mission Control. His interests lie in Distributed Systems with his current focus being Systems for AI/ML applications.

name: Ashwin Sarimin
bio: I am a Platform Lead at DHL Netherlands working on improving technology, culture and people. Specialized in Platform Engineering, Team Topologies and Kubernetes with a strong interest in team dynamics, helping people get the best out of themselves. As someone with Suriname roots living in the Netherlands, I have experienced and understand how important diversity, inclusion and belonging is. Recently became Deep Roots Co-Lead to help people from underrepresented groups achieve more in CNCF.
tagline: Platform Lead @ DHL & Deep Roots Co-Lead

name: Attila Mészáros
bio: Attila Mészáros is a software engineer with over a 15 years of experience designing and building software systems, architectures, and developer tooling. In recent years, he has focused on cloud-native platforms and Kubernetes-based solutions. He currently works at Apple, where he contributes to building data platform as part of the Flink team. He is a co-founder and maintainer of the Java Operator SDK and servers as a member of Operator Framework Steering Committee.

name: Atulpriya Sharma
bio:
Known across the cloud-native community as Maharaj, I make complex technology accessible - from KubeCon stages to community meetups to client boardrooms. What started as a manual QA engineering career over a decade ago has evolved into leading developer relations at scale as a Principal Developer Advocate. 

I combine engineering depth with narrative instinct - debugging a Kubernetes operator in the morning and crafting a developer content strategy by afternoon.
tagline: Principal Developer Advocate @ Improving | CNCF Ambassador

name: August Simonelli
bio: August Simonelli is a Principal Product Manager at Red Hat. He has worked with customers around the world to help them adopt, use, improve, and implement open source technologies. Raised in Boulder, Colorado, August now lives in Sydney, Australia and is a strong advocate for using open source technology to solve real-world problems. He believes that technology has the potential to make a positive impact on the world, and he is committed to helping people use it to make a difference.

name: Aurélie Vache
bio:
Developer Advocate at OVHcloud in France.
She is CNCF ambassador, Docker Captain, Google Cloud Developer Expert, Women techmarkers Ambassador & GitPod Hero.
Developer and Ops for over 20 years.

Conferences organizer since 2016. Technical writer, book author & reviewer, sketchnoter and speaker at international conferences.

She created a new visual way for people to learn and understand Cloud technologies: "Understanding Kubernetes/Istio/Docker in a visual way" in sketchnotes, books and videos.
tagline: Developer Advocate at OVHcloud, Docker Captain, CNCF Ambassador & GDE

name: Austin Abro
bio: Austin Abro is a full-time maintainer of Zarf at Defense Unicorns, a tool built to enable declarative creation & distribution of software into air-gapped/constrained environments. Previously, he worked at Fiat Chrysler as a full stack Java developer before being promoted to technical coach, where he worked with teams to help them improve software engineering practices.

name: Ayato Tokubi
bio: Ayato Tokubi is a software engineer at Red Hat, specializing in container technologies. He serves as a maintainer for CRI-O, an open-source container runtime for Kubernetes. He has contributed to various open-source projects, including Kubernetes.

name: Bailey Hayes
bio: Bailey Hayes is the CTO at Cosmonic and has applied Wasm experience across diverse domains, including building graphics-intensive web applications, User-Defined Functions (UDFs) in databases, IoT solutions, and cloud-native microservices powered by wasmCloud. She wears many hats in the open source ecosystem from standards to implementations as the W3C WebAssembly WASI Subgroup co-chair, Bytecode Alliance TSC Director, and maintainer of CNCF wasmCloud.
tagline: CTO at Cosmonic | TSC Director at Bytecode Alliance | W3C WebAssembly WASI Subgroup Co-Chair

name: Balbir Singh
bio: Balbir Singh is a distinguished engineer at NVIDIA, specializing in Linux memory management. Balbir wrote the initial memory cgroup controller in the Linux kernel and was involved with the development of cgroups. He also wrote the CPU accounting controller and taskstats, and has worked in several areas of the Linux kernel, such as the scheduler and hypervisor. His other interests include security and formal verification.

name: Baruch Sadogursky
bio:
Baruch Sadogursky (@jbaruch) did Java before it had generics, DevOps before there was Docker, and DevRel before it had a name. He built DevRel at JFrog from a ten-person company through an IPO, co-authored "Liquid Software" and "DevOps Tools for Java Developers," and is a Java Champion, a Microsoft MVP for AI, and a CNCF Ambassador alum.

Today he's head of DevRel at Port and a self-certified Level 3 AI Context Sommelier, turning off the lights in your software factory once and for all.

name: Bassam Tabbara
bio: Bassam has created two CNCF-graduated open source projects, Crossplane and Rook, and now leads Modelplane, an open source control plane for AI inference. He is a founding member of the Crossplane Steering Committee, and the CEO & Founder of Upbound, the control plane company.
tagline: Crossplane Steering Committee, Founder & CEO Upbound
role: Crossplane Steering Committee, Founder & CEO Upbound

name: Basundhara Chakrabarty
bio: Basundhara Chakrabarty is a software engineer at Databricks working on networking infrastructure. Previously at Nutanix, she led feature development on Envoy Proxy, including co-authoring the reverse tunnel feature in Envoy 1.36, enabling persistent reverse connections to services behind NAT and firewalls. She has spoken on custom socket interfaces in Envoy at Virtual EnvoyCon 2026. She is working on adopting Dynamic Modules for scalable networking at Databricks.

name: Ben Hirschberg
bio: Ben is a veteran cybersecurity and DevOps professional, as well as computer science lecturer. Today, he is the co-founder at ARMO, with a vision of making end-to-end Kubernetes security simple for everyone, and a core maintainer of the open source Kubescape project. He teaches advanced information security academically in both undergrad and graduate courses. In his previous capacities, he has been a security researcher and architect, pen-tester and lead developer at Cisco, NDS and Siemens.

name: Ben Petersen
bio: Hi, I'm a product manager working at Microsoft on Azure, specifically AKS.  I work primarily with upstream open-source projects.
tagline: Product Manager on Azure Upstream, Microsoft

name: Benjamin Elder
bio: Benjamin Elder is a Senior Software Engineer at Google working on Kubernetes. Ben is a long time contributor to the project since writing kube-proxy's iptables mode for GSoC 2015 and is an elected member of the Kubernetes Steering Committee.

name: Benjamin Wang
bio: Benjamin Wang is a staff software engineer at VMware (acquired by broadcom). He is passionate about open source. He currently is an etcd maintainer and technical lead of sig-etcd. He loves to play Chinese chess in his spare time.

name: Blaine Gardner
bio: Blaine is a Storage Architect at IBM Storage focusing on Ceph storage for the IBM Fusion and Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation (ODF) teams. He is a maintainer of the CNCF-graduated Rook project making sure Ceph and Kubernetes live together in harmony. Their current focus topics are the Container Object Storage Interface (COSI), Multus networking, and object storage integration. Blaine lives in Denver, Colorado and enjoys rock climbing, partner dancing, and coffee.
tagline: Storage Architect, IBM Fusion, OpenShift Data Foundation
role: Storage Architect, IBM Fusion, OpenShift Data Foundation

name: Boteng Yao
bio: Boteng Yao is a Software Engineer at Google, Senior Envoy Maintainer, and Fix Lead on the Envoy Security Team. He specializes in data plane architecture, security, reliability, and AI networking, contributing to both Envoy open source and Google’s production platforms

name: Bowei Du
bio: Bowei has worked in the Kubernetes project as a member of SIG-NETWORK since 2015. He has worked directly on scalability (EndpointSlice, nodelocaldns), APIs and specifications (co-author DNS spec, helped move Ingress to GA (sorry!), initiated the Gateway API project.

name: Brandon Royal
bio: Brandon is dedicated to bringing technical solutions together to drive business outcomes for customers adopting Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a core part of their technology stack.  At Google, Brandon leads go to market strategy for AI on Google Kubernetes Engine, and works closely with customers, partners and internal teams to realize the value of open AI models and tools on Google Cloud AI Infrastructure.

name: Brandon Schoen
bio: Brandon is a Senior Director at Heroku, leading Professional Services and guiding product strategy. Dedicated to customer success, he helps teams design, build, and run applications on a fully managed, cloud-native platform. Brandon collaborates closely with engineering and client teams to empower both professional developers and citizen builders to reach production securely and at scale. Outside of work, he can be found in Las Vegas, NV, plotting his next grill upgrade.

name: Brandt Keller
bio: As a member of the CNCF Technical Oversight Committee, Brandt helps support the technical stewardship and long-term health of the cloud native ecosystem. He is a Staff Software Engineer with a passion for open source, a Cloud Native Ambassador, and a maintainer of the Zarf project within OpenSSF. His work focuses on open source security, cloud native delivery, and producing practical guidance that helps end users adopt secure, resilient platforms.
tagline: CNCF TOC | Staff Software Engineer | OpenSSF Maintainer

name: Braydon Kains
bio: Braydon is a software developer at Google Cloud working on the Ops Agent. Under the GitHub username @braydonk you can find his contributions in Fluent Bit, OpenTelemetry repos, and various auxiliary repos. He is also the creator and maintainer of the yamlfmt tool.

name: Brian Graf
bio: Brian is a Senior Developer Advocate at NetApp Instaclustr. Brian is an author, public speaker, father, tinkerer, and adventurer. When Brian is not working, you can find him spending time with his wife and 7 kids, camping/hunting,  or traveling the world. Brian is ex-EMC, ex-VMware, and ex-AWS.

name: Brian Ugie
bio: Brian Ugie is a Senior Software Engineer at Adobe with over 15 years of experience spanning systems administration, infrastructure automation, and modern cloud engineering. He began his career managing bare-metal Linux environments, where he developed a deep appreciation for the operational discipline that underpins reliable systems at scale.

name: Bridget Kromhout
bio: Bridget Kromhout is a Principal Product Manager at Microsoft Azure, focusing on the open source cloud native ecosystem

name: Brooks Townsend
bio: Brooks is a Senior Lead Software Engineer at Capital One, where he defines and implements platform standards that enable secure, scalable software delivery across the organization. His work focuses on multi-tenancy, platform scalability, and attribute-based access control (ABAC), building reusable patterns that balance developer experience with enterprise governance. He is a frequent speaker at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, DevOpsDays, and Kubernetes Community Days.
tagline: Senior Lead Software Engineer, Capital One

name: Carlos Costa
bio: Dr. Carlos Costa is a Distinguished Engineer at  IBM Research￼, where he leads AI platform initiatives focused on large-scale inference and AI infrastructure. He is a co-founder and maintainer of  llm-d￼, a Kubernetes-native project for distributed LLM inference. With over 20 years of experience in high-performance computing, distributed systems, and cloud-native platforms, Carlos helps advance open, scalable AI infrastructure from research to production.
tagline: IBM Distinguished Engineer -- making gen AI easier to use, more cost-effective and more scalable in the hybrid cloud

name: Carlos Sanchez
bio: Carlos Sanchez is a Principal Scientist at Adobe Experience Manager, specializing in software automation and agentic applications. Involved in Open Source for over 20 years, he is the author of the Jenkins Kubernetes plugin and a member of the Apache Software Foundation amongst other open source groups, contributing to several projects, such as Kubernetes, Jenkins or Apache Maven.

name: Carlos Santana
bio: Senior Specialist Solutions Architect at AWS leading Container solutions in the Worldwide Application Modernization (AppMod). He is experienced in distributed cloud application architecture, emerging technologies, open source, serverless, devops. kubernetes, gitops. He is CNCF Ambassador and contributes to projects such as ArgoCD .  Find him on Twitter @csantanapr or the CNCF Kubernetes Bookclub https://santana.dev

name: Casey West
bio: With over 25 years of experience building internet infrastructure—some of his Perl code even still ships in macOS!—Casey West is a Lead Developer Advocate at Google Cloud. He is passionate about making developers' lives easier by exploring the frontiers of AI engineering and modernizing platform architecture. An experienced international speaker, Casey loves sharing what he's learned about building effective systems and happy teams. He is based in Pittsburgh, PA.
role: Head of AI Infrastructure & Applied Engineering, Developer Relations

name: Catherine Fang
bio: Catherine is a Software Engineer at Google. Catherine is participating SIG instrumentation, focusing on collecting observability signals for Kubernetes clusters.

name: Catherine Paganini
bio: Catherine Paganini is an active non-code contributor, committed to helping make the open source community more welcoming to everyone. Her CNCF journey began with essential resources for newcomers, including founding the CNCF Glossary and co-authoring the CNCF Landscape Guide (V1). From there, she co-founded Merge Forward and KubeCrash. Professionally, she's theHead of Community and Content at Buoyant, the company behind Linkerd, where she champions Linkerd's focus on operational simplicity.

name: Cecil Wöbker
bio: Cecil Wöbker is Co-Founder & CTO at remberg, a Munich-based company building an AI-first platform for industrial asset management. He studied Computer Science at TU Munich and Technology Management at CDTM. Cecil leads remberg's technological development, helping industrial companies digitize maintenance and service processes through cloud-based solutions and AI copilots.

name: Cellan Hall
bio: Cellan Hall is a Software Engineer at Isomorphic Labs, managing observability for clusters running tens of thousands of ML workloads. They instrument Kueue and the Kubernetes scheduler to survive massive spikes from mixed AI compute. Cellan builds telemetry to catch API server bottlenecks before they trigger cascading failures. When not tuning alerts, they are obsessing over extraction times and dialling in the perfect espresso.

name: Chad Swenson
bio: ​Chad Swenson is a Senior Principal Software Engineer, Architect, and Product Owner for platform engineering at AT&T, and a Kubespray maintainer (SIG Cluster Lifecycle). He balances architecture and strategy with hands-on engineering in the trenches of core infrastructure and dev tool platforms. Since 2016, he has scaled a multi-cloud, multi-cluster, multi-tenant Kubernetes platform, abstracting complexity into a fully featured, managed dev experience focused on cluster lifecycles and GitOps.
tagline: Kubespray Maintainer | Senior Principal Software Engineer at AT&T | Platform Engineering & GitOps

name: Chad M. Crowell
bio: Chad is a CNCF Ambassador and Principal SRE at Akamai. Chad is the author of the book "Acing the Certified Kubernetes Administrator Exam." Chad also enjoys teaching Kubernetes in the small community-led group KubeSkills.
tagline: Principal SRE at Akamai, CNCF Ambassador, Speaker, and Author

name: Chase Christensen
bio: What energizes me most is exchanging ideas, learning from others’ challenges, and sharing knowledge that turns ambitious ideas into secure, high-impact solutions. As a Kubestronaut and community builder with the AMLC of the Rockies, I believe the best breakthroughs happen when people learn and build together. Through open-source contributions, enablement programs, and mentoring emerging talent, I thrive on creating connections that help others succeed.

name: Chenyu Zhang
bio: Chenyu Zhang is a software engineer, focusing on the development and maintenance of the CNCF projects Harbor and Dragonfly, with additional experience in DevOps and cloud-native technologies.

name: Chris Aniszczyk
bio: building a better world through open collaboration
tagline: building a better world through open collaboration

name: Chris Burns
bio: Open-source enthusiast, wearer of many hats, but at the core – an engineer, with a specific interest in building platforms, applications and securing the software supply chain. Chris has played almost every core engineering role there is, from software engineering to platform engineering, all the way to architecting and team leading, Chris prides himself in being able to lead the way in many disciplines, but what really drives him is problem solving on the frontier.

name: Chris De La Garza
bio: I'm a Staff Solutions Engineer specializing in zero trust access and identity-aware infrastructure for enterprise environments. I spend my days helping organizations move beyond perimeter-based security and I'm excited to share hands-on patterns from the field at KCDs.
tagline: Staff Solutions Engineer · Zero Trust & Identity-Aware Infrastructure

name: Chris Plank
bio: Chris Plank is a Enterprise Architect, Product Owner and Platform as a Product evangelist working for NatWest Bank in Edinburgh, Scotland. He has been leading a Platform as a Product initiative within the Bank since 2023 working on radically changing the Banks approach to provisioning and maintaining services. Chris contributes to the Open Source Community as one of the CNCF Platform Engineering Technical Community Group Leaders and helping with events including Cloud Native Rejekts and SOOConUK
role: Platform Engineering Leader, Product Owner, Evangelist

name: Chris Pokorni
bio: Chris Pokorni, the founder of NQB8 Cloud Tech Consulting, is an independent Cloud Native instructor and curriculum developer for The Linux Foundation. He advances Kubernetes education by delivering technical training to global audiences through public courses, enterprise programs, and training partners. Chris also develops and maintains self-paced eLearning content focused on Kubernetes and Cloud Native technologies, drawing on extensive experience in enterprise IT and hybrid cloud architecture.
tagline: Cloud Native Instructor & Curriculum Developer @ NQB8 Cloud Tech Consulting

name: Chris Short
bio: Chris Short has been a proponent of open source solutions throughout his 30+ years in various IT disciplines, including systems, security, networks, DevOps management, and cloud native advocacy across the public and private sectors. He is an active Kubernetes contributor and co-leads the Kubernetes Contributor Comms team. Chris is a disabled veteran (US Air Force) living with his wife and son in Metro Detroit. Chris writes about Cloud Native, DevOps, and other topics in his DevOps’ish newsletter
tagline: Principal Trainer, KodeKloud | DevOps’ish | Kubernetes Contributor Comms | Open Source | Corgis | Detroit | Disabled Veteran

name: Christian Heusel
bio:
I am an individual contributor to various FOSS projects, in the CNCF Ecosystem my efforts mostly center around the Kubeflow Community Distribution and the Kubeflow Notebooks v2 Project.

Other than that I also enjoy contributing to the Arch Linux Distribution where I am a Package Maintainer, Bug Wrangler and Infrastructure Admin aswell as various community roles.

Professionally I am available for contracting on DevOps/MLOps topics aswell as training and consulting for any Open Source project.

name: Christian Melendez
bio: Christian helps customers to build fault-tolerant, elastic, reliable, and cost optimized workloads in AWS. Author of Kubernetes Autoscaling book. He’s passionate about Kubernetes, programming, and building tech communities. Christian has spent 19 years working in different companies to build modern solutions using the cloud.
tagline: Principal Specialist Solutions Architect at AWS

name: Christian Posta
bio: Christian Posta (@christianposta) is VP, Global Field CTO at Solo.io. He is the author of "Istio in Action", "AI Gateways in the Enterprise" and many other books on cloud-native architecture. He is well known in the cloud-native community for being an architect, speaker, blogger (https://blog.christianposta.com) and contributor to various open-source projects in the AI and cloud-native ecosystem.
tagline: VP, Global Field CTO at Solo.io

name: Christine Kim
bio: Christine Kim focuses on developer experience at Isovalent @ Cisco, where she dabbles in the world of Kubernetes and Service Meshes.

name: Christophe Sauthier
bio:
Christophe directs CNCF's training and certification programs.
He defines CNCF's vision for courses and certifications, and follows every step of its realization.
Christophe is an Open Source veteran with over 20 years' experience both in the community (Ubuntu, OpenStack, Cloud Native...) and in professional services.
Living in Montreal but originally from France, he enjoys spending time with his wife and children when he's not on the basketball court, his other great passion.

name: Christopher Haar
bio: Christopher is focusing on open source software. He is a regular contributor to open source and a maintainer for providers in crossplane eco-system. He has many years’ experience in the creation of enterprise infrastructure for different industries, from Banking over Telco&Railway to Cloud.

name: Christopher Maher
bio: Christopher Maher is Director of Platform Engineering at Ashley Furniture Industries, where he leads an AI Ops team building on-prem inference infrastructure across NVIDIA and Apple Silicon clusters. He is the creator of LLMKube, an open-source Kubernetes operator for AI model inference. With over a decade in platform and automation engineering, Christopher focuses on making GPU-accelerated AI workloads a first-class citizen in Kubernetes environments.
tagline: Director of AI/ML Operations, Ashley Furniture Industries | Creator of LLMKube

name: Ciara Stacke
bio: Ciara is a Senior Software Engineer at F5 and technical lead of the NGINX Kubernetes networking teams, where she helps shape the technical direction for NGINX Gateway Fabric and NGINX Ingress Controller. A former maintainer of both projects, she is currently focused on the next generation of gateway and ingress capabilities at NGINX, with a particular interest in how AI workloads reshape Kubernetes networking.

name: Colin Griffin
bio:
Colin Griffin is CEO at Krumware, and a Co-Chair of the CNCF Platforms Working Group. Colin Griffin is a software engineer by trade, specializing in cloud-native application and infrastructure development; with an emphasis on developer enablement and platform engineering. He founded Krumware with the goal of enabling companies to build better environments for their developers, through technology development.
Krumware helps organizations build better software.

name: Cong Gu
bio: Frank is a manager at LinkedIn's AI Training Platform team. He has presented LinkedIn's AI platform in multiple settings both internally and externally (including Kubecon).

name: Connor Guerrero
bio: Connor Guerrero is a Senior Developer Relations Manager at Crusoe and one of the founding members of Crusoe’s developer advocates team. He focuses on GPU infrastructure, AI training & inference workflows, and helping engineers build on Crusoe's cloud platform. He has several years of prior experience in the AI chip industry as an ML engineer and field applications engineer, helping teams deploy and optimize workloads on specialized AI hardware.

name: Corey McGalliard
bio: My team and I power and protect life online by building an internal, opinionated Kubernetes platform that meets Akamai's change-safety, security, and compliance expectations while delivering an excellent developer experience. I have had the opportunity to contribute to the CNCF Platforms Community Group Initiatives, updating the Platform Maturity Model and Whitepaper. I believe that computing systems allow me to love my neighbors well by providing excellence in the Cloud Native industry.

name: Cortney Nickerson
bio:
A CNCF Ambassador and Head of Community at Nirmata, Cortney is active in the cloud native space. She leads Kyverno community, co-organizes events like K8s Community Days, serves State of OpenCon Advisory Board, co-hosts podcasts & speaks at international events. She became a techie as employee 7 at a startup acquired by DataDog & learned K8s by writing for the Data on K8s Community.

She advocates for Diversity, Equity & Inclusion, is plagued by imposter syndrome, and does her best to parent

name: Dag Bjerre Andersen
bio: I’m passionate about almost everything related to Kubernetes, and I’ve worked extensively with GitOps over the past few years 🔄 | Speaker at KubeCon, ArgoCon, KCD, and Cloud Native Denmark 🗣️ | Kubestronaut 🚀

name: Dakota Sullivan
bio: Dakota is a staff engineer at The Trade Desk specializing in Kubernetes, and has been building container and cloud infrastructure for 9 years.
tagline: Staff Software Engineer @ The Trade Desk

name: Damini Satya
bio: Damini Satya is a Lead Site Reliability Engineer specializing in Kubernetes, cloud-native infrastructure, and large-scale distributed systems. She leads initiatives that improve platform reliability, developer productivity, and operational excellence across enterprise-scale Kubernetes environments. Her work spans Kubernetes, AWS, CI/CD, observability, and production engineering, with a recent focus on applying AI and LLMs to automate incident investigation and root cause analysis.

name: Damon Cortesi
bio: Damon has a long history in analytics and big data including building social analytics on HBase and MongoDB back in 2010. Since then, he's spent time at AWS on the EMR, Glue, and Athena teams helping customers build and debug Spark, Trino, and HBase environments. These days, he's working at Airbnb building data warehouse infrastructure on Kubernetes.

name: Dan Garfield
bio:
Dan Garfield is a SLC native and VP OSS for Octopus Deploy and Codefresh Co-founder. As an Argo Maintainer, he works parmiarily on Argo CD and Argo Rollouts. He helped create the GitOps Working Group and Open GitOps Principles. He helped create the most popular GitOps certification with Argo CD and writes consistently about best practices for GitOps involving Security, Development processes, and scaling.

Catch him in the Argo documentary!
tagline: Argo Maintainer, Open GitOps Co-Creator, Codefresh Founder

name: Dan Gomez Blanco
bio: Principal Observability Architect at New Relic, driving best practices and operational readiness with end user architectures. Platform engineer since 2011, including CERN and Skyscanner, focusing on OpenTelemetry and operational excellence. Active in the community, I served on the OTel Governance Committee (2023-2025) and maintain the End-User SIG.
tagline: Principal Observability Architect at New Relic, OpenTelemetry End-User SIG Maintainer

name: Daniel Bichuetti
bio: Daniel Bichuetti is Co-CEO and CTO of Forlex, where he leads the engineering of domain-specific AI systems and the GPU infrastructure used to train and serve them. A computer scientist and serial entrepreneur, he works across distributed training, Kubernetes, high-performance networking, data pipelines, and reliable production AI. His focus is turning large-scale infrastructure lessons into practical, reproducible engineering patterns.

name: Daniel Borkmann
bio: Daniel Borkmann co-created eBPF and is a kernel developer at Isovalent working on eBPF, the Linux kernel and Cilium. He is a long-term Linux kernel core contributor in the eBPF and networking subsystem for over a decade and co-maintains eBPF and XDP.

name: Daniel Bruno
bio: Daniel Bruno is a Senior Staff Cloud Engineer at Uber with over twenty years of experience, leading architecture for its multi-cloud, cloud-native portfolio.

name: Daniel Bryant
bio: Daniel Bryant is a platform engineer and PMM at Syntasso. His technical expertise focuses on ‘DevOps’ tooling, cloud platforms, and microservice implementations. Daniel is a long-time coder, platform engineer, and Java Champion who contributes to several open-source projects. He also writes for InfoQ, O’Reilly, and The New Stack, and regularly presents at international conferences such as KubeCon, QCon, and JavaOne. In his copious amounts of free time, he enjoys running, reading, and travelling.
tagline: Platform Engineer and Head of Product Marketing @ Syntasso

name: Daniel Moch
bio: For over 20 years, Daniel has worked as a software engineer in the Defense and Aerospace industry. His experience ranges from embedded device drivers to large logistics and information systems. In recent years, he has focused on helping legacy programs adopt modern DevOps practices. Daniel works with the open source community as part of Lockheed Martin's Open Source Program Office.
tagline: DevOps Architect, Lockheed Martin Open Source Program Office

name: Daniel Oh
bio: Java Champion, CNCF Ambassador & TAG DevEX Co-Chair, Microsoft MVP, Developer Advocate, Technical Marketing, Keynote Speaker, Published Author

name: Danielle Cook
bio: Danielle Cook is a cloud native author, practitioner, and community organizer helping organizations adopt enterprise-ready technologies and communicate their business value. She co-authored and maintains the CNCF Cloud Native Maturity Model, co-chairs the CNCF Cartografos Working Group, and is a CNCF Ambassador. She founded KubeCrash, a bi-annual virtual community meetup, and co-authored Admiral Bash's Island Adventure. She brings the same rigor and pragmatism helping navigate what comes next.
tagline: CNCF Ambassador, Co-Organizer, Cartografos Working Group

name: Danielle Zeis
bio: Danielle Zeis is a principal product marketing manager at IBM, where she works on products across the FinOps portfolio, including IBM Kubecost and IBM Cloudability. Her focus includes cloud cost management, Kubernetes cost allocation and optimization, and helping engineering and FinOps teams better understand the cost and efficiency of cloud-native workloads.

name: Darian DeFalco
bio: Darian DeFalco is a Senior Staff Site Reliability Engineer at Transfix, a SaaS provider of intelligent data and pricing tools for the logistics industry. He focuses on Kubernetes infrastructure, GitOps workflows, agentic workflows, and platform automation. His background includes supporting high-performance research computing at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory and building scalable systems in production environments.
tagline: Transfix, Senior Staff SRE, Core Platform Team

name: Dave Smith-Uchida
bio: Dave Smith-Uchida is a Principal Engineer at Broadcom working on vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS).  Dave has been working on data protection for Kubernetes for the last several years, most recently at Kasten by Veeam.  He is a founding member of the Kubernetes Data Protection Working Group and was formerly the architect for the Velero Open Source Kubernetes backup project.  He has a wide range of experience ranging from embedded systems to supercomputing and cloud systems.

name: David Aronchick
bio:
I am CEO and co-founder of Expanso, the company behind the distributed compute platform Bacalhau. This means I spend most of my time helping humans to convince machines to be smarter. I am only moderately successful at this.

Previously, I led product management for Kubernetes on behalf of Google, launched GKE, and co-founded the Kubeflow project, and led Open Source ML Strategy at Azure. I have also worked at Protocol Labs, Amazon and Chef and co-founded three startups.

bio: TODO

name: David Biel
bio: David Biel is Director of Business Development at R.E. Biel Company, a family owned dental cabinet manufacturer in Texas. A former teacher and band director, he came into manufacturing with no software background and ended up rebuilding the company's web presence and internal systems on cloud-native infrastructure using AI assisted tools. He represents the non-engineer end user the cloud-native community rarely hears from directly.
tagline: Director of Business Development at R.E. Biel Company, a family owned dental cabinet manufacturer
company: R.E.Biel Company, Inc. - Biel Dental Cabinets

name: David Eads
bio: David Eads is a distinguished software engineer at Red Hat and co-lead for Kubernetes sig-apimachinery and TL for sig-auth.

name: David Gohberg
bio: David Gohberg is a Tech Lead at monday.com where he works on building the best CRM on the planet. He has worked across the stack, from embedded networking applications to building web experiences that users will love. When he's not coding, you can find him weightlifting, skiing, reading Japanese manga, and open water swimming.

name: David Jumani
bio:
David Jumani is a Senior Software Engineer at Solo.io. He has experience in virtualization, networking, infrastructure management and cloud security.
He is a Kubernetes SIG sub-project maintainer, committer to an Apache project and an avid open source contributor. 
He loves automating, optimizing and making life easier whenever possible.
When outside the matrix, he's playing Soccer or Rugby, trekking in the wilderness or just soaking up the sun outdoors.

name: David Justice
bio: David Justice leads Azure Container Upstream at Microsoft, where his teams contribute to CNCF and Bytecode Alliance projects that advance AKS. He focuses on open-source AI infrastructure, particularly isolating, scaling, and serving agentic and inference workloads on Kubernetes. Previously he helped bring WebAssembly to cloud-native computing. David maintains several CNCF projects, has co-chaired the CNCF TAG-Runtime Wasm working group, and co-authored "Go for DevOps" (Packt, 2022).

name: David Palilonis
bio: David Palilonis is part of the staff at the CNCF, where he leads membership development and works with organizations worldwide to strengthen the community and support the adoption of cloud-native technologies. He focuses on building partnerships that ensure CNCF remains a vibrant, collaborative home for the projects and practitioners shaping the future of computing.
tagline: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Membership Development

name: David Pech
bio: Accomplished DevOps professional with 20 years of experience in software development and infrastructure management. Proficient in a wide array of technologies within the Kubernetes and CNCF ecosystem, with a focus on producing high-quality, sustainable software solutions. Highly effective in leading hands-on teams to deliver direct value to customers. Passionate about educating and enabling teams in the adoption and understanding of cloud technologies.
tagline: Kubernetes, ArgoCD, AWS, OCI, Postgres fan

name: David Porter
bio: David Porter is a Staff Software Engineer at Google working at the intersection of scalability, security, and Kubernetes extensibility. David works on evolving Kubernetes to meet the intensive resource management demands of modern AI and machine learning workloads. David is also a SIG Node reviewer and the primary maintainer of cAdvisor, the widely used Kubernetes resource monitoring library.

name: David vonThenen
bio: David vonThenen is an AI/ML Engineer where he focuses on production AI systems, enterprise AI strategy, and architectures for explainable, governable, and reliable generative AI. His work spans Agentic AI, Graph RAG, Document RAG, AI memory systems, multi-agent architectures, OpenSearch, Neo4j, data lineage, provenance, and AI governance.
tagline: AI/ML Leader | Keynote Speaker | OSS Engineer & Developer Advocate | Agentic AI, Deep Learning, Production AI | Python, Go, C++

name: Dawn Chen
bio: Dawn Chen is a principal software engineer at Google. Dawn has worked on Kubernetes and Google Container Engine (GKE) before the project was founded. She has been one of tech leads in both Kubernetes and GKE. Prior to Kubernetes, she was the one of the tech leads for Google internal container infrastructure -- Borg and Omega for 6 years.

name: Decheng Dai
bio: Decheng Dai is a Member of Technical Staff on Anthropic's Core Infrastructure team, where he has built two generations of the Kubernetes scheduler that places inference, training, and research workloads across the company's TRN, TPU, and GPU fleet. Before Anthropic he spent six years on Google's Borgmaster team, focused on TPUv1 bring-up and network-aware scheduling.

name: Deepak Choudhary
bio: Deepak Choudhary, is part of the Data Science Platform team within Nvidia. He is working on the Observability side of the Platform, to support and develop solutions for the next 10x data scale.
tagline: Senior Systems Software Engineer, Data Platform Nvidia

name: Deepak Goel
bio: Deepak is a technology leader specializing in cloud-native platforms, Kubernetes, distributed systems, and platform engineering. As CTO for Cloud Native at Nutanix, he leads cloud-native strategy, platform architecture, and modern infrastructure initiatives. He has helped drive Kubernetes adoption, scalable data services, and the development of KUDO, later donated to the CNCF, enabling enterprises to modernize applications and operate reliably at scale across hybrid and multi-cloud environments.

name: Deepak Kinni
bio: Deepak specializes in Cloud Native Storage, focusing on architecting and developing the vSphere CSI driver to enable seamless storage provisioning. He designs and implements Cloud Native Data Protection solutions, including backup and restore workflows for Kubernetes workloads. As a Kubernetes contributor, he leverages his expertise in distributed systems and storage architecture to deliver robust solutions.

name: Dheeraj Kapur
bio: none

name: Diana Todea
bio: Diana is a CNCF Ambassador and Operational Resilience TAG lead, co-leads the Neurodiversity Merge Forward community, and organizes Cloud Native Days Romania. Professionally, she is the Head of Developer Relations Engineering at VictoriaMetrics, where she works at the intersection of developer experience, observability, and open source community engagement.
tagline: CNCF Ambassador and Head of DevRel
role: Head of DevRel Engineering, CNCF Ambassador

name: Diana Zawadzki
bio: Diana Zawadzki is a Software Engineer on Uber’s Cadence team, focused on durable workflow orchestration, AI-native developer tooling, and reliable long-running systems. She contributes to Cadence’s open-source ecosystem and previously worked on Uber’s Java Monorepo and AI/ML Platform infrastructure teams. Diana studied Computer Science at Stanford with a focus on operating systems and distributed systems.

name: Dibyo Mukherjee
bio: Dibyo Mukherjee is a Lead Engineer at Adobe working on agentic platforms, cloud efficiency, and capacity management. Previously, he worked on cloud CI/CD and API management at Google. He is a maintainer and governing board member for Tekton, the cloud native CI/CD framework, and was previously a maintainer for Spinnaker.

name: Dilpreet Bindra
bio:
Dilpreet Bindra is the Senior Director of Engineering for the VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) division at Broadcom, where he leads the delivery of runtime platforms, automation, and modern cloud-native architectures. He is a passionate advocate for bridging the gap between developer agility and enterprise IT governance, with a current focus on integrating Kubernetes and Private AI infrastructure into enterprise environments.

A seasoned engineering leader, Dilpreet’s expertise spans both hardware and software systems. Prior to his long tenure shaping core VMware technologies—including ESXi and vCenter—he held software and hardware engineering roles at Sun Microsystems and HP. Within the open-source community, he actively champions Broadcom’s Platinum membership in the CNCF and drives continuous upstream collaboration.

Dilpreet holds a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering from Stony Brook University. Outside of his engineering work, he is a basketball player, hiker, pickleball player, and dedicated father.

name: Dipanwita Guhathakurta
bio: Dipanwita Guhathakurta is a software engineer at IBM specializing in performance simulation, latency modeling, and capacity planning for LLM inference serving platforms.

name: Divine Odazie
bio:
Divine Odazie is a CNCF Ambassador, founder of EverythingDevOps, and a Program Committee member for Platform Engineering Day NA 2026. As a Developer Advocate, Divine helps cloud native vendors build better tools and infrastructure.

With experience contributing to Kubernetes, Cilium, etc., Divine has given talks and workshops at conferences like KubeCon NA, Open Source Summit EU, KCDs, and Ansible Contributor Summit.

Divine also supports the cloud native community in Africa as an organizer.

name: Divya Mohan
bio: Divya is a Lead Open Source Advocate at SUSE, where she contributes to the company's open source projects. She co-chairs the documentation for the Kubernetes project & also serves on its Code of Conduct committee. She previously worked extensively in systems engineering. bio:

His work focuses on the operational side of Cilium at scale: keeping the datapath fast, safe to upgrade, and transparent to the workloads on top.
