A frequent speaker at AWS re:Invent, HashiConf, DevOpsDays, and Grace Hopper Celebration, she shares practical lessons from experimenting, building, and shipping under pressure.

name: Jago Macleod
bio: Jago Macleod is an Engineering Director at Google, where he leads much of the Kubernetes and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) team, which gives him the opportunity to work with some of Google Cloud’s largest customers. Prior to working at Google, Jago helped make the smart homes that may eventually turn against us at Nest; and before that, he made some of the games that will distract us along the way as VP of Engineering at Disney Interactive Games.

name: Jake Hulberg
bio: Jake Hulberg is the Founding Developer Advocate at Infisical, the open source security platform for secrets, certificates, privileged access, and AI agent access. He creates demos, videos, and guides that teach developers how to manage secrets securely, run PKI, and control privileged access, for both people and AI agents. He also runs Jake's Tech (@jakestechjourney) on YouTube.

name: Jake Pineda
bio: Open source, cloud-native, and AI strategist driving ecosystem growth for the Linux Foundation and CNCF. I design engagement models that bring the world's largest companies into community governance and turn complex technical needs into sustainable revenue. Actively shaping the intersection of AI and cloud-native infrastructure through conformance, policy, and adoption frameworks. Financially rigorous, equity-minded, and backing the movement across Latin America and underserved communities.
tagline: Open Source Growth Strategist, Senior Membership Executive, CNCF

name: Jakub Scholz
bio: Jakub is a CNCF Ambassador and engineer at Cloudera with deep expertise in Kubernetes, streaming, and messaging. As a co-founder and maintainer of the Strimzi project, he has spent years bridging the gap between Apache Kafka and cloud-native infrastructure. Before his time at Cloudera, Jakub worked at Red Hat and in the financial sector, bringing a wealth of real-world operational experience to the open-source community.

name: Jakub Suchy
bio: Jakub Suchy is the Director of Solutions Engineering at HAProxy Technologies, where he designs and prototypes solutions for application delivery and load balancing infrastructure. With his background in Linux infrastructure and Open Source Applications, he specializes in developing innovative approaches to modern application delivery challenges, focusing on micro-services architecture and high-availability systems

name: James Spurin
bio:
James Spurin, a CNCF Ambassador, Docker Captain and a Technical Course Creator has educated over 100K students in Cloud Native, DevOps and Kubernetes.

His 25-year career includes management, engineering and software development at Nomura, Goldman Sachs, Dell EMC, and Demon Internet.

As a trusted figure in Cloud Native, James combines his extensive experience with his passion for teaching to promote understanding and adoption of cloud native technologies.
tagline: CNCF Ambassador, Docker Captain, Founder and CEO of DiveInto

name: Jamie Danielson
bio: Jamie is a Senior Software Engineer at Honeycomb where she works on instrumentation libraries and agent observability. She is an active contributor to multiple OpenTelemetry projects, and a maintainer for OpenTelemetry JavaScript.

name: Jan Bronicki
bio: Jan Bronicki is a software engineer at Microsoft and a maintainer of Flatcar Container Linux, a CNCF project that provides a minimal, secure, and immutable operating system for running containers at scale. He is passionate about open source, cloud native infrastructure, and building reliable systems through collaboration. His work spans operating system maintenance, automation, security, and community-driven development.
role: Flatcar Container Linux Maintainer | Software Engineer

name: Jan Wozniak
bio: Jan is a software engineer who spends most of his time with open-source technologies. He contributed to and helped to maintain various parts of the Kubernetes ecosystem.

name: Janet Kuo
bio: Janet Kuo is a Senior Staff Software Engineer at Google Cloud and a member of the Kubernetes Steering Committee. She has been shaping Kubernetes since before its 1.0 launch in 2015. She is the co-chair and Tech Lead of SIG Apps, leads Kubernetes AI Conformance, and is a KubeCon co-chair emeritus. When not immersed in Kubernetes, she enjoys exploring the world through travel and photography.

name: Jared Watts
bio: Jared Watts is a Founding Engineer at Upbound, where he is working on advancing cloud-native computing by enabling anyone to build their own cloud platform. He is also a co-creator of the open source Crossplane (https://crossplane.io) and Rook (https://rook.io) projects. Prior to Upbound, Jared worked on P2P storage distributed across the public internet at Symform, a startup later acquired by Quantum. Jared began his career at Microsoft working on applications for Windows Server management.

name: Jason Deal
bio: I'm a software engineer at AWS, working on EKS Auto Mode and Karpenter

name: Jason Plumb
bio: Jason Plumb (he/him) is a hacker, artist, experimenter, polyglot programmer, and dad from Portland, OR, USA. He is co-maintainer of OpenTelemetry Android and an approver in various OpenTelemetry java projects. When not at work, Jason volunteers with Futel to install and maintain a network of free public payphones. He also builds synthesizers, experiments with sound, screens classic cult films, and rides steel-frame bicycles.
tagline: OpenTelemetry maintainer / Splunk senior principal engineer

name: Jason Schechner
bio: SRE with a career older than the term "SRE".  I've done it all, seen it all, and (hopefully) learned at least a few lessons along the way.  Life-long tinkerer, habitual puzzle-solver, SCUBA diver and enthusiast for anything interesting.
tagline: Traversal's First SRE Researcher and AI Adoption Engineer

name: Jason Stryker
bio: Jason is a engineering leader with extensive experience implementing Kubernetes and Cloud Native technology in highly regulated environments. As the Community of Practice lead for Kubernetes at Capital One, he exudes a deep passion for open source and community governance models exemplified by CNCF hosted projects.
tagline: Kubernetes Community of Practice Lead @ Capital One

name: Jay Jackson
bio: Jay Jackson is a Senior Software Engineer at CallRevu, based in Houston, Texas. He brings over 2 decades of experience in the tech industry, primarily as QA and Software Engineer. Jay has navigated this tech journey as a deaf individual, with American Sign Language (ASL) as his primary mode of communication and is passionate about exploring ways to improve accessibility for Deaf and Hard of Hearing community.

name: Jayanth Varavani
bio: Jayanth is a Software Development Manager on the AWS EKS Networking team. He has several years of experience in the networking domain and serves as a maintainer of the EKS CNI and Network Policy project. Jayanth is deeply passionate about eBPF and actively leads multiple eBPF-related initiatives within EKS. You can find him on GiHub as @jayanthvn
tagline: AWS, Software Development Manager at EKS
role: Software Dev Manager - EKS Networking and Node runtime

name: Jed Salazar
bio: Jed Salazar started his Security and SRE journey working on Borg clusters and securing Alphabet companies at Google. He's passionate about security and SRE and spreading knowledge to benefit everyone in the community. In his free time, he enjoys trail running the mountains of Boulder, Colorado.

name: Jeff Hoffman
bio: Jeff Hoffman is a Vice President at Oracle, where he leads the Container, Kubernetes, and Serverless organization for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). His team is responsible for OCI services including Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE), Container Instances, and Functions. Jeff has over 30 years of experience in cloud and engineering leadership, including work prior to Oracle at Amazon, Samsung, HashiCorp, and Dell.

name: Jeff Spahr
bio: Jeff Spahr is a Director in the AI/ML organization at Capital One, focused on scaling high-performing infrastructure and platform teams. A long-time Kubernetes enthusiast, his passion for infrastructure spans global-scale cloud deployments to the Raspberry Pi cluster in his home office. Jeff enjoys sharing lessons learned at conferences like KubeCon, SREcon, and All Things Open. He lives in Raleigh, NC, with his wife and two children.
tagline: Director, AI/ML Infrastructure & Platform - Capital One

name: Jeffrey Sica
bio: Jeffrey (@jeefy) is Head of Projects at the CNCF, with a focus on improving community and project automation. Before that, he worked at Red Hat and the University of Michigan focusing on Cloud Native technologies and CI/CD patterns. Jeffrey has been a contributor to upstream Kubernetes, helping in SIG-Contribex, SIG-Release, and SIG-UI. He passionately advocates for open source development and recognizing and alleviating burnout.

name: Jeffrey Ying
bio: Jeffrey is a contributor to Kubernetes, mainly working in the SIG apimachinery and CLI space. He had led and been involved with many features such as Server Side Apply, Aggregated Discovery, and OpenAPI V3.

name: Jeffry Hernández
bio: Senior SRE @ Wizeline with a strong background in cloud infrastructure and Open Source technologies. Co-organizer of CNCG Cali and KCD Colombia. Last year He has been deeply involved in Al Infrastructure, helping customers to serve models at scale and implement best observability practices.

name: Jennifer Weir
bio: Jennifer Weir is a Kubernetes Platform Engineer at Ford Motor Company, where she focuses on cloud infrastructure at scale, cluster automation, resource management, and platform reliability. She holds a B.S. in Computer Science from the University of Michigan–Ann Arbor.

name: Jenny Vega
bio: Jenny Vega is a Senior ML Platform Engineer at Isomorphic Labs, building the infrastructure for AI-driven drug discovery. Specializing in Kubernetes orchestration, Jenny designed and rolled out scheduling enhancements that boosted GPU cluster utilization across tens of millions of monthly runs. Previously, she was a Senior Solutions Architect at Google and AWS, guiding enterprises and startups on distributed training and large-scale cloud architectures.
tagline: Senior ML Platform Software Engineer @ Isomorphic Labs

name: Jeroen van Erp
bio:
Jeroen van Erp is a Technology Advocate at SUSE, active open source contributor, and Cloud Native speaker, helping developers and platform engineers build open, portable, and resilient infrastructure.
With a background spanning engineering, architecture, and product management, he distills complex topics like Kubernetes, observability, cloud-native security, and open source, into actionable insights.
When not on stage, he's a Rancher at heart, herding his sheep in the Netherlands.

name: Jesper Joergensen
bio: Started in 2024 with Brian Grant and Alexis Richardson to rethink how configuration for software infrastructure is managed. Before ConfigHub, Jesper was a product leader at Heroku, API product manager at Salesforce, and later ran Twilio's Voice & Video business. His work has centered on platform-as-a-service and developer tools, and on the gap between the elegant experience developers get when writing code and the far rougher experience of operating it.

name: Jesse Butler
bio: Jesse is a product manager for Amazon EKS focused on helping customers do more with Kubernetes. He started his career in software more than two decades ago, working up the stack from driver development into userspace and container runtimes. He's been working with containers for several years, and has contributed to the OCI specifications and the Kubernetes release team.

name: Jessica Forrester
bio: Jessica Forrester is a Senior Distinguished Engineer and the Chief Architect for AI Catalyst Engineering at Red Hat, working at the intersection of AI and cloud native as new technologies move into the Red Hat AI product portfolio. She was an early contributor to Red Hat OpenShift, Kubernetes, and their related communities. She has led many cross-functional engineering teams at Red Hat across AI, hybrid cloud services, and Kubernetes / OpenShift Container Platform.
tagline: Senior Distinguished Engineer & Chief Architect AI Catalyst Engineering, Red Hat

name: Jian Cheung
bio: Jian is a Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic working on large accelerator clusters. Prior to Anthropic, Jian worked on Compute Infrastructure at Airbnb.

name: Jian Li
bio: Jian Li is currently working as a principal research engineer at SK Telecom (SKT), and he is also serving as a member of ONOS TST at Open Networking Foundation (ONF). He previously worked as an open source developer at ONF. Jian is currently serving as the chief architect for the Petasus AI Cloud project, which aims to deliver cost-efficient, high-performance AI infrastructure optimized for heterogeneous AI workloads, including both training and inference.
tagline: Building AI-Ready Kubernetes Infrastructure for On-Prem and Beyond

name: Jim Beyers
bio: Hey there! I'm Jim on the CVS DevEx team, blending my love for tech with making life easier for developers. After stints at Target and Capital One, I've learned to connect tech and business. Originally from Wisconsin, I landed in Minneapolis and collected degrees like Pokémon cards (BA in CS, MS in Software Engineering, MBA from St. Thomas). Off hours, I'm with my wife Nora, kids Amelia and Ben, and our husky Cali Bean. Big on music, concerts, films, and Age of Empires 2.

name: Jim Bugwadia
bio: Jim Bugwadia is a co-founder and the CEO of Nirmata, the Kubernetes policy and governance company. Jim is an active contributor in the cloud native community and currently serves as co-chair of the Kubernetes Policy and Multi-Tenancy Working Groups. Jim is also a co-creator and maintainer of Kyverno, the policy engine built for Kubernetes.

name: Jing Chen
bio: Jing Chen is a software engineer at IBM Research, where she works on Generative AI infrastructure, benchmarking, and capacity planning for distributed LLM inference on Kubernetes. She is a contributor to open-source projects including llm-d using AI-native simulation methodologies.

name: Jing Hu
bio: Software Engineer building observability platforms at eBay

name: JJ Jordan
bio: JJ Jordan is a Member of Technical Staff on Cohere’s Internal Infrastructure team, where he builds orchestration, scheduling, and reliability systems to improve utilization of large-scale GPU training clusters. He previously spent 17 years at Microsoft working on Visual Studio, Azure observability, and distributed systems built on Kubernetes.
tagline: Member of Technical Staff at Cohere

name: Joe Betz
bio: Joe Betz is a tech lead of the Kubernetes api-machinery SIG. Joe has contributed to extensibility features including custom resources, admission webhooks, and CEL. Joe has also contributed to etcd as a project maintainer.
role: Engineering Lead and SIG API Machinery TL

name: Joe Julian
bio:
Joe Julian is a Senior Technical Lead at Omniva, building self-service Kubernetes platforms for AI training and inference on bare-metal GPU clusters. His work spans multi-tenancy, networking, storage, and infrastructure lifecycle management.

A Helm contributor, he uses Flux, GitOps, and custom operators to deploy infrastructure and applications. He uses AI agents for development, testing, documentation, and operations.

Outside work, he enjoys sailing and building useful things.

name: Joe Kutner
bio: Joe is co-founder of the Cloud Native Buildpacks project, which aims to make containerization more secure and more developer friendly. He started the project in 2018 while working as DX Architect at Salesforce Heroku, and today is the DX Architect for Salesforce’s Hyperforce platform. He’s also the author of The Health Programmer.
tagline: Architect at Salesforce, Co-founder of Buildpacks

name: Joe Lanford
bio:
Joe is a Senior Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat and leads the OpenShift Operator Framework team. His primary focus is on designing and building OLMv1 and related tooling to make Kubernetes package management as simple, secure, and flexible as OS package management.

In addition to his work in Operator Framework projects, he has been active in the upstream kubebuilder, controller-runtime, and controller-tools projects.

If you have controller or CRD questions, I (hopefully) have answers!
tagline: Red Hat - Senior Principal Software Engineer - Operator Framework

name: Joe Zhou
bio:
Joe is a cloud-native advocate for storage systems and former startup CTO who excels at leading and motivating team members to deliver exceptional results.

He currently serves as the Lead Developer Advocate in North America at JuiceFS (a high-performance distributed file system) and helps AI/ML engineers, developers, and platform teams get the most out of JuiceFS for performance and efficiency.

name: Joe Nathan Abellard
bio:
Joe Nathan Abellard is a Senior Software Engineer on the Cloud Native Compute Services (CNCS) Platform Engineering team at Bloomberg, and a maintainer of the CNCF Karmada project. He's the lead engineer and product owner for Bloomberg's large-scale, managed multi-cluster Kubernetes platform, built on Karmada, enabling the firm's engineering teams to meet the organization's high-availability (HA) mandate across distributed
infrastructure, without requiring deep multi-cluster expertise.
tagline: Senior Software Engineer, Bloomberg | CNCF Karmada Maintainer

name: Johan Fylling
bio: I've been working as a software developer in the IAM space since 2008. In 2021 I joined The OPA team.

name: John Belamaric
bio:
John is a Sr Staff SWE, co-chair of K8s SIG Architecture and K8s WG Device Management, helping lead efforts to improve how GPUs, TPUs, NICs and other devices are selected, shared, and configured in Kubernetes. He is also co-founder of Nephio, an LF project for K8s-based automation, and a maintainer of CoreDNS, a CNCF project for DNS-based service discovery.

John holds three patents, and is co-author of "Learning CoreDNS" from O’Reilly and "OpenStack Cloud Application Development" from Wiley.
tagline: Google, Kubernetes SIG Architecture and WG Device Management Co-chair

name: John Howard
bio: John Howard is a Senior Architect at Solo.io and Istio Technical Oversight Committee member.

name: John Kastner
bio: John is an applied scientist at AWS who has been working on the Cedar policy language since its inception three years ago. Prior to that he worked on open-source tooling for semi-automated conversion from C into Checked C, a spatially-memory-safe variant of C, after graduating from the University of Maryland with a masters degree in computer science.
tagline: Cedar Dev and Senior Applied Scientist at AWS

name: John Kjell
bio: John is an Engineering Manager at Docker, building an agentic software factory to patch all the things. Previously at ControlPlane, he helped security-conscious organizations build and assure mission-critical platforms. He is a member of the in-toto Steering Committee and maintainer of the Witness and Archivista projects. He also serves as a co-chair of the CNCF's TAG Security. In the OpenSSF, John is a member of the inaugural Ambassador cohort and contributes to the SBOMit project.

name: Johnu George
bio: Johnu George is a Technical Director at Nutanix specializing in machine learning systems and cloud-native AI platforms. An active open-source contributor, he has led collaborations across Kubeflow, KServe, and Knative. His interests include ML systems and distributed learning infrastructure. He is a maintainer of KServe and Envoy AI Gateway, and Co-Chair of the Kubeflow Training and AutoML Working Group.

name: Jon Huhn
bio: Jon Huhn is a Software Engineer at Microsoft working on CNCF projects like CAPZ and DRA in Kubernetes.

name: Jonathan Bryce
bio: Jonathan Bryce is the Executive Director of Cloud & Infrastructure at the Linux Foundation, where he leads both the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and the OpenInfra Foundation—two of the largest and most influential open source communities in the world. With over 15 years of open source leadership, Jonathan co-founded the OpenStack project, guiding its evolution into a global ecosystem that supports a multi-billion-dollar market and serves as the de facto standard for open cloud infrastructure. Before his open source career, Jonathan spent over a decade in data center infrastructure and co-founded one of the industry’s earliest cloud computing companies, which grew into a billion-dollar business following its acquisition by Rackspace. Passionate about open collaboration, infrastructure innovation, and empowering users, contributors, and ecosystems worldwide, Jonathan frequently speaks at international conferences on open source strategy, infrastructure modernization, cloud-native technologies, and open source AI initiatives.

name: Jonathan Norris
bio: Jonathan Norris is Director of Software Engineering at Dynatrace, leading feature management engineering after Dynatrace acquired DevCycle, the developer-first feature management platform he co-founded and led as CTO. He serves on the OpenFeature Governance Board, helping advance vendor-neutral feature flagging standards, and focuses on progressive delivery, continuous deployment, release safety, and measuring what matters.
tagline: Director, Software Engineering @ Dynatrace · OpenFeature Governance Board Member · Formerly Co-Founder & CTO, DevCycle

name: Jooho lee
bio: Jooho Lee is a Toronto-based technology professional with over a decade of experience at Red Hat, working across cloud-native platforms and AI. He is on the OpenShift AI Model Serving team, integrating KServe and LLM-D into Open Data Hub to enable production-grade, Kubernetes-native deployment and operation of AI/ML models. He is also a KServe committer, contributing to the project’s model serving and LLM inference.

name: Jordan Keister
bio: Jordan is a maintainer for the Operator Framework project and a FOSS contributor for over a decade.  He works with Red Hat helping folks reason about cluster installables and the ecologies required to make them sustainable.

name: Jordan Liggitt
bio: Jordan Liggitt is a software engineer at Google, and helps lead Kubernetes authentication, authorization, and API server efforts.

name: Jorge Castro
bio:
Jorge O. Castro is a community engineer, specializing in Open Source. He's basically a cat herder – a combination of engineering, developer relations, and user advocacy. 

These days Jorge is the Technical Program Management Director at the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, where he's tasked with helping make open source sustainable. He has worked on Ubuntu, Kubernetes, Kubeflow, Cloud Custodian, and Project Bluefin.
tagline: Let's keep the modern world running, sustainably.

name: Jorge Palma
bio: Jorge is the Principal PM Lead for AKS where he serves thousands of customers and mission critical application and helped lead the service to become the fastest growing service in Azure’s history. Formerly he was the Technical Lead for App Dev and DevOps with the Azure Global Black Belt team and has implemented and architected solutions in Azure since 2012, spanning across different roles from Services, Tech Evangelism and Tech Sales. He holds a MSc in Computer Engineering.
role: Principal PM Lead, Azure Kubernetes Service

name: Joseph Sandoval
bio: Joseph Sandoval is a platform engineering and distributed systems practitioner with 25 years across SRE, DevOps, cloud-native infrastructure, and production operations. He focuses on making AI/ML and agentic workloads safe to run on shared platforms through isolation, identity, observability, policy, cost controls, and developer self-service. He is a member of the CNCF Technical Oversight Committee and Vice Chair of the CNCF End User Technical Advisory Board.
tagline: Adobe Inc, Principal Product Mgr, Developer Platforms

name: Josh Berkus
bio: Josh Berkus is the Kubernetes Community Manager, working in Red Hat's Open Source Program Office.   He's currently involved with Kubernetes, Etcd, Elekto, Podman, and uBlue, but has spent more than 20 years contributing to many projects, including Linux, OpenOffice, PostgreSQL, and Django.  He lives in Portland with a librarian, a pottery studio, and an absurdly large cat.

name: Juan Bernal
bio: Juan Bernal is a Staff Engineer at CVS Health, specializing in web development and feature flagging platforms. With a strong background in software engineering practices, he drives library adoption and advocates for web standards. Passionate about innovation, he enjoys exploring new technologies and methodologies. Outside of work, Juan has a soft spot for soft serve ice cream.

name: Juan David Arguello Plata
bio:
Juan David is a leader with experience in cloud-native computing, software development, and IT infrastructure. He serves as the Lead of the Open-Source Program Office at Bancolombia.

Regarding his academic background, Juan David is doing a MSc in CS at the University of Bath, UK, and has a postgraduate degree in AI and ML from The University of Texas at Austin. He is also an active contributor to the tech community who holds the title of Kubestronaut.

name: Juho Syrjänen
bio:
🤝 A Platform Engineer
💛  GitOps 

An infrastructure and platform engineer with over 10 years of experience spanning datacenters, DevOps consulting, and platform development. Juho has spent the past several years helping teams tame complex systems and build resilient platforms.

Currently, Juho is working as a Platform Engineer at ŌURA, where he’s building an internal developer platform supporting smart rings worn by millions. .

name: Jui-An Huang
bio: Jui-An Huang is also known as rueian on GitHub. He is the creator of rueidis/valkey-go, an official Redis/Valkey Go client, and more recently has been contributing to Ray and KubeRay since 2022.

name: Julia Furst Morgado
bio:
Julia helps teams improve system reliability, observability, and scalability by guiding the adoption of modern infrastructure and operational practices.
Beyond her work, Julia is a a Community Manager to the OpenTelemetry project, CNCF Ambassador, AWS Container Hero, Docker Captain, Google Women Techmakers Ambassador, and Girl Code Ambassador. She’s an active community leader who helps organize KCD NY, AWS Community Day NY, and the Cloud Native Meetup NYC.

name: Juliano Costa
bio: Juliano Costa is a Developer Advocate with a focus on OpenTelemetry. He is a CNCF Ambassador passionate about fostering the Cloud Native community and spreading OTel's word everywhere he goes. Juliano is an active contributor to the OpenTelemetry project and a maintainer on the OpenTelemetry Demo, as well as on the Developer Experience SIG. When he's not talking about OTel, you'll find him chasing after his energetic 3-year-old son.
tagline: CNCF Ambassador | Principal Developer Relations Engineer at Dash0

name: Juliano Martinez
bio: Principal Engineer at Adyen with 25 years of experience in Linux, networking, large-scale infrastructure, and automation. His work spans cloud-native platforms, Kubernetes, service networking, observability, and distributed systems. An open-source enthusiast and Go developer, he approaches systems from first principles and builds simple, composable tools that reduce operational complexity.

name: Julie Gunderson
bio: Julie Gunderson has spent over a decade in tech in leadership and developer advocacy roles at AWS, PagerDuty, Gremlin, and Freeman & Forrest. Her work spans reliability, incident response, DevOps, and community building. She founded and organized DevOpsDays Boise for five years. After years speaking about psychological safety and burnout, she is pursuing a master’s in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, shifting her focus from reliable systems to the well-being of the people who run them.

name: Julien Semaan
bio: Julien is the VP of Research & Development at Kubex and a Tech Lead with the CNCF TAG for Developer Experience. With deep roots in open source and cloud-native systems, he has been working with Kubernetes since 2017 and has led multiple product transitions to cloud-native architectures.
tagline: VP R&D @Kubex | CNCF TAG DevEx Tech Lead

name: Juraci Paixão Kröhling
bio: Juraci Paixão Kröhling is a software engineer at OllyGarden, a maintainer of the OpenTelemetry project, a member of the project's governing board and CNCF Ambassador. He has presented about distributed tracing, OpenTelemetry, and other related topics at conferences like KubeCon, OpenSource Summit, FOSDEM, and a few DevOpsDays, among others. Previously, he was also a maintainer of both the OpenTracing and Jaeger projects, having also delivered talks about those projects.

name: Justin Garrison
bio: Justin is a tinkerer and Field CTO and Sidero Labs. He builds ridiculous contraptions and shares them on the internet to make people smile. He also helps companies solve real world infrastructure problems at large and small scales.

name: Justin Munoz
bio: Justin is a Principal Software Engineer helping teams run Kubernetes workloads with confidence. He’s passionate about making the ‘right way’ the easy way, so teams can spend more time shipping and less time fighting the platform.
tagline: Principal Software Engineer, Kinexys by J.P.Morgan

name: Justin O’Leary
bio: Justin OLeary is a security researcher who focuses on cloud-native infrastructure vulnerabilities. His work on confused deputy flaws in Kubernetes operators has uncovered privilege escalation paths in Config Connector, AWS Controllers for Kubernetes, Azure Service Operator, Crossplane, and other major projects. He is presenting related research at Black Hat USA 2026. By day, he serves as Principal Bioinformatics Engineer at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

name: Kai-Hsun Chen
bio: Kai-Hsun leads infrastructure at Hark, spanning compute, data, and the full model lifecycle. Previously, he worked on infrastructure at xAI and Anyscale. He is also an open-source enthusiast who maintains several projects, including Ray, KubeRay, and Apache Submarine, and has been contributing actively to Kueue over the past few months.

name: Kanika Rana
bio: Kanika is a software engineer at Red Hat, where she has been contributing since 2021. She currently works on Argo CD as part of the GitOps team, focusing on scalable and reliable deployment workflows. Prior to this, she worked on the Developer Sandbox — a self-service platform for evaluating OpenShift.

name: Karena Angell
bio: Karena Angell is a Senior Principal Technical Strategist, Global Engineering at Red Hat focusing on cloud native workloads for Kubernetes, open source software projects, agentic transformation and is the Chair of the CNCF Technical Oversight Committee.
tagline: Senior Principal Technical Strategist, Global Engineering
role: Senior Principal Technical Strategist, Global Engineering

name: Karim Alibhai
bio: Karim once ran a Kubernetes cluster from his basement and will find a way to bring it up in conversation. He loves building tools for other engineers, helping teams move faster, and writing that extra bit of code that makes someone's day. He's worked across infrastructure and application development, always with an eye for making software a pleasure to use. These days, he's obsessed with managing DuckDB on Kubernetes and playing Resident Evil. He considers both to be survival horror.

name: Karol Szuster
bio: Software Engineer with 6+ years of experience. Previously built solutions for AI-driven data publication and curation. Currently at Google developing Kueue to enhance AI training and inference capabilities across Kubernetes clusters.

name: Karol Szwaj
bio: Karol is a senior software engineer at Kubermatic, a maintainer of the Envoy Gateway and kube-bind projects, and is currently working on kcp. He specialises in open-source technologies, distributed systems, and networking, and brings a telecommunications background from university. Karol is an active contributor to the open-source ecosystem, with involvement in projects such as Kyma, Kubermatic, and several CNCF initiatives, including Istio, Envoy Gateway, Kube-OVN, kcp, and Kubernetes SIGs.

name: Karunasri Garigipati
bio: Karunasri(Karuna) Garigipati is a Lead Software Engineer at Heroku(Salesforce), working on Fir, Heroku’s Kubernetes-based platform. She started in observability, learning how platforms fail. Now she builds one, making the infrastructure that runs customer apps scalable, reliable, and secure. She also built Heroku’s AI-powered observability MCP server and wrote about it on the Heroku Engineering Blog. She has a photographic memory for faces. Unlike your logs, she has unlimited retention.

name: Kashif Khan
bio: Kashif Khan is a co-chair of CNCF TAG Infrastructure and maintainer of the CNCF project Metal3.io for 6 years. He works as an open source Architect for Ericsson Software Technology, Finland. He holds a PhD in Computer Science. Kashif is a research and open source enthusiast and his current area of interest is kubernetes deployments on baremetal systems in distributed cloud scenarios.
role: Co-Chair CNCF TAG Infrastructure, Maintainer, Open Source Architect

name: Kaslin Fields
bio: Kaslin Fields is a Developer Advocate at Google Cloud, a Container enthusiast and creator of tech comics. She uses her knowledge of DevOps technologies and methodologies to help others as they enter the Cloud Native world. By creating comics about DevOps tech, she hopes to make learning Cloud Native fun and accessible to everyone!

name: Kasper Borg Nissen
bio: Kasper is a CNCF Ambassador, former KubeCon+CloudNativeCon Co-Chair, Golden Kubestronaut, KCD Organizer, and CNCG Group Organizer. He co-founded Cloud Native Nordics to unite meetups across the region. At Dash0, he helps make observability easy for developers by advocating for better tooling, best practices, and seamless integrations. Bridging observability and platform engineering, he ensures developers stay productive and gain actionable insights exactly when needed.
tagline: Principal Developer Advocate at Dash0, former Co-Chair KubeCon+CloudNativeCon EU/NA, CNCF Ambassador, Golden Kubestronaut, KCD Organizer, Meet-up organizer

name: Kat Cosgrove
bio: Kat is an open source advocate focused on the growth and nurturing of open source through authentic contribution. In particular, her specialties are approachable 101-level content and deep dives on the history of technology, with a focus on DevOps and cloud native. She was the Kubernetes Release Lead for 1.30 Uwubernetes, and currently serves as a member of the Kubernetes Steering Committee, the Release Team Subproject Lead, and a SIG Docs Tech Lead.
tagline: Kubernetes Steering Committee | SIG Docs | SIG Release

name: Kathan Kashiparekh
bio: Senior software engineer at Salesforce building a robust and scalable Integration Testing platform while making it an easy and user friendly experience
tagline: Senior Member of Technical Staff at Salesforce

name: Katherine Druckman
bio: Katherine Druckman is a senior technologist, speaker, and longtime advocate for open ecosystems. Currently Head of Community and Partnership Engagement at JetBrains, she specializes in developer experience, combining software ecosystem strategy, content strategy, and community building, grounded in a foundation of hands-on software engineering experience and proven leadership. She is a long-time open source advocate, developer, and podcaster, and is currently the host of the Reality2.0 podcast.
role: Head of Community and Partnership Engagement

name: Kathryn Baldauf
bio: Kathryn is a software engineer at Apple, where she works on Apple's open source Container and Containerization projects. She has been working in the open source container ecosystem for the past 7 years.

name: Katie Meinders
bio: Katie is a Community Outreach Manager at Isovalent @ Cisco who has spent nearly a decade in the cloud native community. She works closely with the Cilium and eBPF communities, focusing on the content and community engagement helping people discover and understand these projects and get involved.

name: Kavitha Daula
bio: Kavitha Daula is the VP of Engineering at Edera, where she leads the development of secure, high-performance container runtime technologies. Previously, she was Senior Director at GEICO, driving innovations in OS, containers, and language runtimes, including a custom Linux distro for secure workloads. With two decades of experience, she focuses on building developer-friendly platforms that balance strong isolation, performance, and usability.

name: Kaynan Coelho
bio: Kaynan is a Brazilian Engineering Manager at Nubank, based in Fortaleza, Ceará. He leads teams responsible for large-scale data and observability platforms processing petabytes of telemetry data daily. His work focuses on engineering leadership and reliability at scale. At Observability Summit North America, Kaynan shares executive and technical insights from achieving an 8x reduction in query latency on Nubank’s internal logging platform.

name: Kazuki Sato
bio: Kazuki Sato is a software engineer at NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS, Inc., specializing in cloud-native distributed systems and GPU infrastructure. He serves as Lead Architect for GoAT (GPU over APN Testbed), developing nationwide distributed AI platforms leveraging IOWN APN. He also holds a Maritime Officer license — making him one of the rare engineers who handles both physical and digital containers, at least in theory.

name: Keith Babo
bio: Keith Babo is the Chief Product Officer at Solo.io, where he leads product strategy and execution, enabling enterprises to build and scale the next generation of cloud-native and agentic infrastructure for AI-driven applications. Prior to Solo.io, Keith held leadership roles in product management and engineering at Red Hat, Sun Microsystems, and Intel Corporation.

name: Keith Mattix
bio: Keith is a Senior Architect at Solo.io serving as a lead on the Agentgateway project and a member of the Istio Technical Oversight Committee.

name: Kevin Cochrane
bio: Kevin Cochrane is a 25+ year pioneer of the digital experience space. Kevin co-founded his first start-up, Interwoven, in 1996, pioneered open source content management at Alfresco in 2006, and built a global leader in digital experience management as CMO of Day Software and later Adobe. Kevin has also held senior executive positions at OpenText, Bloomreach, and SAP. Now at Vultr, Kevin is working to build Vultr's global brand presence as a leader in the independent cloud platform market.

name: Kevin Dubois
bio: Kevin Dubois is often featured as a (keynote) speaker at conferences around the world, where he shares his passion and knowledge about developer experience, agentic AI, open source, cloud native development and Java. He is also an author, java Champion, and an accomplished software architect and platform engineer. Kevin currently works as a Senior Principal Developer Advocate at IBM, and is also Technical Lead for the CNCF Developer Experience Technical Advisory Group.
tagline: Senior Principal Developer Advocate at IBM

name: Kevin Hannon
bio: Kevin Hannon is focused on improving AI/ML experience on Kubernetes. He started his career as a computational scientist and has always been interested in large scale batch jobs. He is motivated to improve Kubernetes in this area to benefit various use cases that are underserved by Kubernetes.

name: Kevin Klues
bio: Kevin Klues is a distinguished engineer at NVIDIA. He is a former shadow member of the CNCF TOC and a sig-node maintainer, having helped design and implement the CPU, Device, and Topology Managers, Multi-Instance GPUs, and Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) in Kubernetes. Kevin holds a bachelors from Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology, a masters from Washington University in St. Louis, and a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. When not working, you can find Kevin with his kids or enjoying a beer in the sun.

name: Kim Schaefer
bio:
Kim Schaefer is a Senior DevOps and Cloud Engineer focused on Kubernetes, GitOps, and secure platform engineering. She designs and operates production Kubernetes platforms with a focus on deployment reliability and automation in constrained environments.

Kim's work centers on building GitOps platforms that teams can trust in production, especially where change must be deliberate and defensible. She is an open-source contributor and has previously spoken at Open Source Summit and GrafanaCON.

name: Krishna Rekapalli
bio: Krishna Teja Rekapalli is a Sr AI Engineer at IBM watsonx DataLabs, specializing in enterprise LLM-powered AI and agentic workflows. With 7+ years in production ML, he has architected RAG systems across financial services, healthcare, and manufacturing. He works at the intersection of research and practice, with deep experience in the open-source AI ecosystem including Docling, OpenSearch, and K8s.
tagline: Sr AI Engineer, IBM watsonx DataLabs

name: Kuba Tużnik
bio: Kuba is a Senior Software Engineer at Google. He has been maintaining Cluster Autoscaler since 2019, and took on the position of Kubernetes SIG Autoscaling co-chair in 2025. Within the SIG, Kuba's main area of expertise is Node autoscaling.
tagline: K8s SIG Autoscaling Lead | Senior Software Engineer @ Google

name: Lachlan Evenson
bio: Lachlan is a Principal Program Manager on the open source team at Azure. As an emeritus Kubernetes steering committee member and release lead, Lachlan has deep operational knowledge of many Cloud Native projects. He spends his days building and contributing to software that addresses key challenges in the Cloud Native ecosystem. @LachlanEvenson
tagline: Principal Product Manager - Cloud Native Ecosystem

name: Lakmal Warusawithana
bio: Lakmal Warusawithana is a maintainer of OpenChoreo, a CNCF Sandbox project, and a Distinguished Engineer at WSO2. He has led the design of scalable cloud-native developer platforms for enterprises. Previously, he served as VP of the Apache Stratos PaaS project and co-founded thinkCube, where he helped build cloud platforms for telecom operators. Lakmal is a frequent speaker at industry conferences on Kubernetes, platform engineering, and cloud-native architectures.

name: Lasse Vierow
bio: Spent the last few years working in cloud engineering and enjoy cloud native. Participated in the Linux Foundation Mentorship Program and like to explore new technologies, sharing ideas, and connecting with people from around the world.

name: Laura Lorenz
bio: Laura Lorenz is a software engineer at Google. She is an active member of Kubernetes’ upstream focused on SIG-Multicluster, SIG-Node, and releases.

name: Laura Luttmer
bio: Laura Luttmer is a Product Manager at Bindplane, an OpenTelemetry-native pipeline management platform. She has over 10 years of product experience spanning SaaS, legal, and data platforms, and currently focuses on the tooling and patterns that help teams get more out of their observability data.

name: Lebin Cheng
bio:
Serial entrepreneur with multiple successful exits: cofounder of Netskope (IPO) and cofounder of CloudVector(acquired by Imperva/Thales). 
Proven track record of building companies to deliver first in class solutions to meet emerging security needs of enterprise customers. 
Over 20 years in the field of cyber security. Proven track record of working with open source communities.

name: Lee Calcote
bio: Lee Calcote is an innovative product and technology leader, passionate about empowering engineers and enabling organizations. As Founder of Layer5, he is at the forefront of the cloud native movement. Open source, advanced and emerging technologies have been a consistent focus through Calcote’s tenure at SolarWinds, Seagate, Cisco and Schneider Electric. An advisor, author, and speaker, Calcote is active in the community as a Docker Captain, Cloud Native Ambassador and Google SoC Mentor.

name: Leigh Capili
bio:
Leigh is an empathetic speaker and developer with niches in cloud-native systems and security. He has a background in building software to manage infrastructure.

Leigh authored kubeadm’s etcd mTLS implementation and Flux 2’s multi-tenant security model.

Leigh worked with the VMware Tanzu Advocacy team and previously built Developer Experience and Platform with Weaveworks, Beatport, AT&T, and DIRECTV.

Leigh and his wife enjoy snowboarding and have a 60lb dog named Pepsi.

name: Léonard Suslian
bio: I build infrastructure services for bare-metal GPU kubernetes clusters.
tagline: Software Engineer, Compute Infrastructure - Mistral AI

name: Leonardo Grasso
bio: Based in Sicily, Leonardo is passionate about R&D, software design, and building open source tools that engineers enjoy using. He has been working in security by accident since 2020 and is a Falco Core Maintainer. He also leads Sysdig’s open source team, overseeing its work on Falco and Wireshark.

name: Lev Andelman
bio: I am a Linux sysadmin that woke up one morning to a world of DevOps. I was lucky to be part of small companies that grew to a huge scale through insane outages. Those outages took my sleep but awarded me with experience. Today I am Hashicorp Ambassador, Israel Hashicorp User Group co-organizer, DevOpsDays Tel Aviv co-organizer and CTO at cloud and devops consulting company.

name: Lin Sun
bio: Lin is the Head of Open Source at Solo.io, contributing full-time to the open-source community. She serves on the CNCF Technical Oversight Committee (TOC), is a CNCF Ambassador, and is a maintainer for Istio, kgateway, and kagent. An international speaker at tech conferences, Lin frequently blogs about gateways, service meshes, cloud-native connectivity, and AI agents. She is the author of “Sidecar-less Istio Explained” and “AI Agents in Kubernetes”, and holds more than 200 patents.

name: Lior Lieberman
bio: Lior is an engineering lead at Google working on Google Compute Engine and Cloud Service Mesh. He is a leading maintainer of ingress2gateway, and an active contributor to Kubernetes SIG network focused on Gateway API.

name: Liqian Luo
bio: Liqian Luo is a Partner Software Engineering Manager at Microsoft, where she leads the advanced services on top of vanilla Kubernetes: multi-cluster management to manage clusters at scale, AKS Automatic to simplify cluster operations, and most recently, AI infra on Kubernetes. Prior to working at Microsoft, she built various large scale data services including cloud asset inventory, cloud tracing, friend recommendations, just to name a few, at Google.

name: Liudmila Molkova
bio: Liudmila Molkova is a Software Engineer at Google working on OpenTelemetry. She is a member of the OpenTelemetry Technical Committee and a maintainer of the Semantic Conventions. Previously, she led observability efforts for Azure client libraries at Microsoft. Liudmila co-authored distributed tracing implementations across the .NET ecosystem, including HTTP client instrumentation and Azure Functions.
tagline: Software Engineer at Google, Member of the OpenTelemetry Technical Committee

name: Liz Rice
bio:
Liz Rice is Chief Open Source Officer at Isovalent, now part of Cisco. She is an award-winning speaker, and author of O'Reilly books on "Container Security" and "Learning eBPF". She represents Maintainers on the CNCF governing board, and was previously chair of the Technical Oversight Committee, Co-Chair of KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, and on the board of OpenUK.

Liz loves riding bikes in places with better weather than her native London, and making music under the pseudonym Insider Nine.
tagline: Chief Open Source Officer, Isovalent @ Cisco

name: Logan Koch
bio: Software Engineer with over 15 years experience. Co-leads Merge Forward's Friends of Dorothy working group. Active member of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing working group.

name: Long Nguyen
bio: Long Nguyen is a Machine Learning Engineer at the Philadelphia Phillies. He started his career as a quantitative analyst building predictive and generative models to aid in-game strategies. Today, he’s developing framework and toolings to manage and deploy model pipelines at scale.
tagline: ML Engineer at The Philadelphia Phillies

name: Lorenzo Biava
bio: Lorenzo Biava a Staff Infrastructure Engineer at LiveKit, where he operates a global WebRTC network pushing over 10 PB of monthly real-time traffic across dozens of regions. He previously served as Principal Engineer at Microsoft and Nuance, building secure, globally-distributed Kubernetes platforms for Voice AI in strictly regulated environments.

name: Lu Zhang
bio: Lu Zhang is an engineer at OpenAI focused on large-scale AI infrastructure. He currently works on inference systems and previously helped build and operate GPU clusters on OpenAI's Fleet team. His interests span Kubernetes, cloud-native platforms, distributed systems, reliability engineering, and machine learning infrastructure. He is passionate about scaling infrastructure for AI workloads and enabling reliable, efficient operation of GPU-accelerated clusters in production.
tagline: Member of Technical Staff, LLM Inference, OpenAI

name: Lucas Fernandes Martins
bio: I'm a software engineer at Mistral working on Inference.

name: Lucas Käldström
bio: Lucas is a Kubernetes and cloud native contributor since 10 years. He was a CNCF Ambassador for 7 years, awarded Top CNCF Ambassador 2017 with Sarah Novotny. Lucas was a co-lead for SIG Cluster Lifecycle, co-created kubeadm, and ported Kubernetes to ARM. Lucas has been running meetups and KCD Helsinki in Finland, co-created the meetup collective Cloud Native Nordics and has spoken at 10 KubeCons. Lucas is now researching control plane access control as a Staff Software Engineer at Upbound.
tagline: Kubernetes & Cloud Native Developer and Speaker

name: Lucy Sweet
bio: Lucy is a Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic and co-lead of the Kubernetes Node Lifecycle Working Group.
tagline: Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic

name: Luiz Scheidegger
bio: Luiz is an engineer at Anthropic on the Claude Managed Agents team, building the sandboxing infrastructure that runs Claude agents. Before that he was Head of Engineering at Lindy.ai and an engineer at Nextdoor, where he built Launch Control, the company’s experimentation platform. Earlier he worked at Facebook and Uber.

name: Lukasz Ciukaj
bio: With over 10 years of industry experience, Lukasz initially specialized in networking but four years ago, he transitioned into software, cloud technologies, and applications world, with a particular interest in Observability. He has gained valuable expertise in tools like AppDynamics, ThousandEyes, Splunk, and OpenTelemetry, enhancing his technical skill set. He enjoys sharing his knowledge with others on multiple platforms, including blog articles on Splunk.com and LinkedIn posts.
tagline: Observability Solutions Architect, Cisco Splunk | OpenTelemetry Enthusiast | Cloud Native RTP Community Organizer (part of CNCF)

name: Maciej Szulik
bio: Maciej has spent more than 20 years building software and hasn't lost his curiosity yet. By day, he’s tackling Kubernetes challenges for Defense Unicorns. By night, he’s a Python tinkerer working on side projects. A firm believer in the "always be learning" mindset, he balances his technical life with a love for photography and a deep stack of books.

name: Maciej Wal
bio: Maciej Wal is a Cybersecurity Platform Architect at the Cybersecurity Center at MSU Denver, where he designs and operates a cloud-native SOC platform serving multiple community partners across rural Colorado on a $1,000/month budget. He trains student engineers who now maintain the platform in production, and has placed graduates into DevOps and security roles across industry. His work spans GitOps, zero-trust architecture, and observability.
tagline: Cybersecurity Platform Architect, The Cybersecurity Center at MSU Denver

name: Maciek Różacki
bio: Product manager behind K8Ss and GKEs capabilities for Scalability, HPC, Batch and AI Training use cases. Figuring out how to make Kubernetes a the best platform to build research platforms.

name: Maia Iyer
bio: Maia is an Advisory Software Engineer at IBM Research specializing in platform engineering and cloud-native security. While deeply experienced in zero trust - a dedicated maintainer of SPIFFE's Tornjak project - her research now tackles the infrastructure demands of the AI era. An active and passionate speaker and blogger, Maia now explores the intersection of agentic workloads and Kubernetes, and how cloud-native platforms must evolve to make AI agents run reliably and securely.

name: Manabu McCloskey
bio: Manabu is a Solutions Architect at Amazon Web Services. He focuses on contributing to open source application delivery tooling and works with AWS strategic customers to design and implement enterprise solutions using AWS resources and open source technologies. His interests include Kubernetes, GitOps, Serverless, and Souls Series.

name: Manfred Moser
bio: Manfred Moser is a Senior Principal DevRel Engineer at Chainguard, bringing a profound focus on software supply chain security to the open source world. A dedicated community leader and published author, he brings decades of technical expertise as a software engineer and advocate. He has a deep, influential history with the Apache Maven ecosystem, including authoring prominent reference books, and is an active Trino maintainer, advocate, and podcast host.
tagline: Open source coder, mentor, educator, and advocate

name: Marcin Gwozdz
bio:
Proactive IT solutions professional advisor with combined business and technical knowledge: experienced in cross-sector enterprise software sales, building technical alliances, and supporting channel sales for years. Focused on open-source solutions, always ready to share knowledge.

My vision is that open source will be as sustainable in terms of product and revenue growth as proprietary solutions, as more and more entrepreneurs will work on open source projects.

name: Marcin Wielgus
bio: Marcin Wielgus is a Staff Software Engineer at Google. Marcin joined the company in 2010 and since then he has been working on various projects, ranging from Android applications to recommendation engines. He started contributing to Kubernetes before the 1.0 release and currently leads the K8S batch team at Google.

name: Marco Martinez
bio: I lead community strategy at Coder, building programs that connect developers, open source users, and the business. My path into community is a little unconventional, with a background spanning video games, social, video, paid media, SEO, and content. Today, I bring those experiences together to grow community, strengthen product feedback loops, and show how community can drive adoption and business impact.

name: Marcos Hernández
bio: Marcos is a Distinguished Engineer with Isovalent@Cisco and works on Kubernetes NEtworking and Datacenter networking solutions and products

name: Marek Pelka
bio: Marek Pelka is an engineering manager at monday.com, where he leads platform engineering initiatives, including the company's internal developer portal. Based in Warsaw, Poland, Marek focuses on developer experience and infrastructure tooling at scale.

name: Marek Siarkowicz
bio: Marek is a Staff Software Engineer at Google, SIG-etcd tech lead, approver in API machinery, and contributor to Kubernetes scalability. He began his career at Warsaw startups, where he developed a passion for open source and extreme programming

name: Marino Wijay
bio: Marino Wijay is a Canadian, Traveller, International Speaker, and Open Source Advocate and Architect for AI, API Platforms, Service Mesh, Kubernetes, and Networking. He is a CNCF Ambassador,  Organizer for KCD Toronto, and Founder of EmpathyOps. He is passionate about technology and modern distributed systems. He will always fall back to the patterns of Networking and the ways of the OSI. Community building is his driving force; A modern Jedi Academy.
tagline: Engineered Solutions - Networking, APIs, Kubernetes, AI

name: Mariusz Sabath
bio: Mr. Sabath is a Senior Technical Staff Member on the AI Platforms team at IBM Research, with extensive experience and a long track record in cloud-native security. He is Project Lead for Kagenti, an open-source Kubernetes platform for AI agents, a SPIFFE Steering Committee member, and manages IBM's open source contribution process. His work focuses on Zero Trust for agentic workloads—workload identity, authorization, and secure tool access. He holds nearly 30 patents.
tagline: Senior Technical Staff Member in IBM Research

name: Mark Rossetti
bio:
Mark Rossetti is a software engineering focusing on open-source projects at Microsoft and is also the co-chair of Kubernetes' SIG-Windows. 
Mark focuses on improving the experience of using Windows containers in Kubernetes. 
Mark has also served on the Kubernetes release team since v1.25 and was the Enhancements Lead for v1.27

name: Marlow Warnicke
bio: Marlow is a Senior Engineer at NVIDIA and a chair for CNCF TAG Workloads and the CNCF Batch Subproject. Marlow has expertise in resource management, the AI/ML Kubernetes cloud compute ecosystem, embedded systems, high performance compute system tools, kernel drivers, tracing libraries, and security. Marlow's interests lie in optimizing the cloud native ecosystem for both heterogeneous systems and also for HPC/AI/ML compute with an eye for both performance and efficiency.

name: Marly Salazar
bio: I am a software engineer with a heavy background in legacy and on premises systems, and migrating those to the cloud, modernizing and automating them. I have been working on the kubernetes project for a year and a half, primarily on kubectl.

name: Maroon Ayoub
bio: Maroon Ayoub is an AI infrastructure architect at Red Hat focused on distributed inference. He co-leads development of llm-d and specializes in scaling LLM inference with Kubernetes-native architectures, KV-cache orchestration, and open source integrations.
tagline: Senior Principal Machine Learning Engineer, Red Hat
role: Senior Principal Machine Learning Engineer, Red Hat

name: Mary Campbell
bio: With more than 30 years of experience in technical services and account management, Mary helps organizations worldwide using open source software to create new opportunities, products, and experiences. The Linux Foundation offers flexible training, rigorous certifications, and engagement options for varied needs and budgets. Its expanding education portfolio supports Linux, cloud native, security, decentralized trust, AI, networking, and other high-demand technology fields.
tagline: Linux Foundation Education, Sr. Manager Education Solutions

name: Masato Kozuka
bio: Masato Kozuka is a Platform Engineering and Security specialist at Hitachi, Ltd., where he leads architecture for the company's enterprise AI agent platform enforcing least-privilege access across diverse clients, agents, and users. He is also a Backstage organization member, plugin maintainer, and Keycloak contributor whose Backstage plugin abstracts Keycloak OIDC integration for platform teams. He brings the same philosophy to this session: make secure-by-default access a platform primitive.
tagline: Hitachi, Ltd., Member of Technical Staff,  Platform Engineering & Security Specialist

name: Mathew Wicks
bio:
At NVIDIA, Mathew works with critical open-source projects and their maintainers to enable success on current and future NVIDIA platforms.

Independantly, Mathew serves on the Kubeflow Steering Committee and leads the development of the Kubeflow Notebooks sub-project.
tagline: Open Source Developer Relations @ NVIDIA | Kubeflow Maintainer

name: Mathis Felardos
bio: Mathis Felardos is an Inference Software Developer at Mistral AI for the past two years, with a main focus on Disaggregated Serving and other infrastructure-based optimizations for LLMs. He is a maintainer of the LeaderWorkerSet and DisaggregatedSet projects.

name: Matt Boersma
bio: Matt has worked with software systems since the 1980s in a variety of capacities, focusing recently on cloud and container technologies.

name: Matt Dering
bio: Matt Dering, PhD is a Machine Learning Engineer in the Philadelphia Phillies R&D department. Prior to that he got his PhD in Computer Science at Penn State in 2018, specializing in Machine Learning in Engineering Design.
tagline: ML Engineer At The Philadelphia Phillies

name: Matt Farina
bio: Matt works as Head of Portfolio Architecture and Community at SUSE. He is a maintainer on Helm and Artifact Hub. Matt is an author, speaker, and regular contributor to open source.
tagline: Head of Portfolio Architecture and Community
role: Head of Portfolio Architecture and Community

name: Matt Heon
bio: Matt is one of the core maintainers of Podman and leads the team working on Podman, Buildah, and Skopeo at Red Hat. He's worked on Podman since the project's inception. In his off time, he enjoys baking and reading.

name: Matt Lord
bio: Matt Lord has spent the last 25+ years working in the database space both as a producer at MySQL and MongoDB and as a consumer at WeWork and Etsy. Today he leverages these decades of experience to help make Vitess the best Open Source solution for running MySQL at scale and supporting the PlanetScale team as we revolutionize the database developer experience.

name: Matt Matejczyk
bio: Matt is a Software Engineer at Google, working on GKE and Kubernetes. He also serves as the chair of the Workload Aware Scheduling Working Group (WG-WAS).

name: Maxime Coquerel
bio:
In my current role at Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), I lead the Kubernetes Security program, overseeing security architecture, cloud threat research, threat modeling, and risk assessment of cloud designs and patterns. 

Additionally, I collaborate closely with our strategic partners, cultivating and sustaining business relationships with third-party providers, including cloud vendor teams and emerging cloud security startups.
tagline: Director | Principal Cloud Security Architect | CNCF Ambassador | Microsoft MVP Azure & Cloud Security

name: Medya Ghazizadeh
bio: Master of computer science from DePaul University in Chicago,  minikube maintainer since 2019 and author of multiple open source projects and 6K contributors to Kubernetes (top 25 all time)

name: Mengjin Yan
bio: Mengjin Yan is a Ray committer and engineering lead for Ray Core at Anyscale, where she helps shape the evolution of Ray’s foundation layer. Her work includes task event infrastructure, label-based and topology-aware scheduling, and improvements to Ray Core’s scheduling and observability. Before Anyscale, she spent seven years at LinkedIn building large-scale online storage and distributed database systems.

name: Mengxuan Li
bio:
Maintainer of HAMi community
Approver of volcano community

Responsible for the development of gpu virtualization mechanism on HAMi and volcano. Working on providing device-sharing on all heterogeneous devices and improving device utilization on clusters.

name: Mert Toslali
bio: Mert Toslali is a Staff Research Scientist at IBM Research, where he focuses on optimizing training and inference pipelines for generative AI at scale. He holds a Ph.D. from Boston University and works at the intersection of systems and AI. He brings a deep background in systems research for platform engineering and is an experienced speaker, having presented his work at venues such as MLSys, SoCC, the PyTorch Conference, and other leading technical venues.

name: Mesut Oezdil
bio: Mesut Özdil is a DevOps engineer based in Germany and the Tech Lead of CNCF’s TAG Infrastructure. He holds the CKA, CKS, and CDP certifications, is a Nebius AI CloudOps Engineer, and was selected for Nebius’s inaugural Fellowship cohort. His work spans Kubernetes infrastructure, GPU virtualization, and observability. He is a core contributor to Project HAMi, a CNCF Sandbox project bringing GPU sharing and overcommit protection to Kubernetes, and contributes to the open source projects.

name: Micah Hausler
bio: Micah is a Principal Engineer at AWS, focused on Amazon EKS and Kubernetes security

name: Michael Amundson
bio: Michael Amundson is a distinguished engineer in the Developer Experience organization at CVS Health where he leads technical direction for the CAP Application Platform. His near decade of experience in platform engineering started at Target Corporation, where he helped build Target's in-house application platform. Prior to his work on platforms, Michael worked as an application engineer in roles across a number of Fortune 500 companies, daydreaming of platforms that didn't yet exist.

name: Michael Aspinwall
bio: Michael is a software engineer at Google and has been contributing to Kubernetes, DRANet and other OSS initiatives. His background consists of Kubernetes, Networking, and has been working in the field as both a consumer of Kubernetes and maintainer. His primary focus as of present is Scalability and how to push Kubernetes past its current limits.

name: Michael Bolot
bio: Michael has worked for the last four years in the Kubernetes Ecosystem. He currently works on multi-cloud compute and networking at GEICO and previously worked at SUSE on Rancher (specializing in RBAC, API Frameworks, and Virtual Clusters).
tagline: Senior Staff Software Engineer at GEICO

name: Michael Crenshaw
bio: Michael Crenshaw is a Staff Software Engineer on the Argo CD team at Intuit. He is the most active contributor to the Argo project, focusing on security and performance improvements in Argo CD. He helps maintain Intuit’s ~50 Argo CD instances and ~20k Argo CD applications.

name: Michael Friese
bio: Michael is a Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft, specializing in Kubernetes, containers, eBPF, networking, and security. He is currently contributing to Inspektor Gadget, an open-source observability, security and debugging tool under the CNCF.

name: Michael Irwin
bio:
Michael Irwin has been a developer for ~20 years and a part of the container space since 2016. He's passionate about making development easier for all and breaking down complex concepts into simpler ideas. 

He previously worked in the university setting for 11 years and has been on Docker's DevRel team for ~4.5 years. He loves educating, pushing boundaries, and learning from others.

Outside of work, you'll find him spending time with his family of eight kids or trying to enjoy the outdoors.

name: Michael Kinsley
bio: Michael Kinsley is Director of GEICO's Hybrid Cloud Fabric, a multi-provider zero-trust platform based on Istio, Cilium, and SPIFFE/SPIRE. He set the vision and hired the team that built it. His dream was always an org that gives back to the community, not just one that consumes it, and he's finally living it.
tagline: Hybrid Cloud Fabric - Agent of Chaos

name: Michael Levan
bio: Michael Levan translates technical complexity into practical value. He is an AI Architect, solutions engineer, and content creator in the AI and Platform Engineering space who spends his time working with organizations around the globe on technical implementation and strategy. Michael is also a Microsoft MVP, 4x published author, podcast host, international public speaker, CNCF Ambassador, and was part of the Kubernetes v1.28 and v1.31 Release Team.
tagline: Building High-Performing Agentic and Kubernetes Environments | AI Architect | CNCF Ambassador | 4x Published Author & International Public Speaker

name: Michael McCune
bio: Michael McCune is a software developer creating open source infrastructure and applications for cloud platforms. He has a passion for problem solving and team building, and a lifelong love of music, food, and culture.

name: Michael Zazula
bio: Mike is an engineer on the ML tooling team within Capital One. His primary focus is on building reusable tools and components across the Machine Learning Development Lifecycle for Data Scientists within the Org. Mike lives in New Jersey with his wife. Outside of work, his hobbies include home renovations (electrical, plumbing, tiling, etc.), gardening, and most recently has taken up beekeeping.
tagline: Lead Machine Learning Engineer @ Capital One

name: Michael Rishi Forrester
bio: Michael Forrester is a student, explorer, and educator at the boundary between humanity and technology. Over 25+ years he's gone from CTO to IC across operations, AI, cloud, and platform engineering, including time at AWS, ThoughtWorks, Red Hat, and Honeywell. His training has reached over a million engineers. He speaks at KubeCon and CNCF on Claude Code, MCP, and AI safety for platform engineers. Tools don't transform organizations. People do.
tagline: Preparing Tomorrow's Innovators, Elevating the Average

name: Michas Szacillo
bio: Michas is the Engineering Team Lead of Bloomberg’s Streaming Platform. The platform, which is running on Kubernetes, serves as the foundation for many of Bloomberg's data streaming use cases. Michas is also a frequent collaborator to the CNCF community, with contributions to projects including Karmada and KServe. He currently serves as a core maintainer of Karmada.

name: Micheal Kingston
bio: Micheal Kingston is a Product Manager at F5 who works on NGINX projects that help users manage application traffic in Kubernetes environments. He drives projects NGINX Ingress Controller and NGINX Gateway Fabric. Micheal was previously a software developer and DevOps engineer, and he spent several years working as a solutions architect for NGINX. He has a strong interest in modern applications, Kubernetes, and cloud-native technologies.

name: Michele Mancioppi
bio: Michele has active in the observability space for more than a decade. Former staff engineer turned PM and then back, he likes to code tracing instrumentation, Kubernetes operators and Infrastructure-as-Code integrations for observability almost as much as asking "Why would you need that?".
tagline: I am a man of simple tastes: I like my software boring, and my observability easy and powerful.

name: Michelle Au

He has been a member of the Kubernetes release team for many releases, including as the communications coordinator and docs lead. He is interested in building healthy, sustainable communities and scalable distributed systems, and working collaboratively to drive positive change.

bio: Mike leads observability at ClickHouse, where he works on ClickStack, a developer-focused observability platform. He joined ClickHouse through the acquisition of HyperDX, a company he co-founded, after spending five years building tools for engineers and gradually becoming a database person along the way. Now, he focuses on improving open-source observability tooling, from polishing buttons and docs to optimizing search and ingestion infrastructure.

bio: Mike Stefaniak is a Senior Manager of Product at AWS, where he leads product strategy for containers. His team focuses on simplifying Kubernetes for platform engineers and application developers at scale, spanning compute elasticity, workload abstraction, and cluster governance.

bio: Mike Wilson is a Principal Architect at Adobe, leading a 200,000+ virtual-core migration onto OpenShift and advising GPU and LLM-inference strategy. The through-line of his career is placement and scheduling at scale — from one of the largest OpenStack deployments in production (~20,000 nodes) and the Nova scheduler upstream, to GPU placement today. He lives in Alpine, Utah, trains Brazilian jiu-jitsu, and reads widely across theology, philosophy, and geopolitics.

name: Mitch Connors
bio: Mitch Connors is a Principal Software Engineer at Microsoft, and serves on the Istio Technical Oversight Committee. Over the past 17 years, Mitch has worked at Google, F5 Networks, Amazon, an Industrial IoT startup, and State Farm Insurance, giving him a broad perspective on the needs of Enterprise Software Developers. This experience has given Mitch a passion for bringing technological innovation to the long tail of technology adopters without the need to start from scratch.

name: Mofesola Babalola
bio: Mofesola Babalola is a Site Reliability Engineering leader at Tempo Software, managing observability and service mesh systems for over 5 million users. Expert in Kubernetes, Istio, ArgoCD, and Flux, he specializes in resilient platforms and automation. Mofesola has led production ambient mesh adoption and GitOps workflows, sharing practical insights at the intersection of DevOps, SRE, and developer experience.

Mofi Rahman (@moficodes) is a Developer Advocate at Google. His favorite programming language these days is Go. Maintainer of Metal3 project, with strong expertise in Kubernetes, Cluster API, and infrastructure automation. bio: Muhammed Yunas Chirayath is a Site Reliability Engineer with production experience building and operating large-scale platforms on OpenShift and Kubernetes. He specializes in observability strategy, cost optimization, and platform reliability. He has led efforts to build unified observability platforms, reduce telemetry waste, and solve hard networking and reliability problems that rarely make it into documentation but always show up in production.

bio: Nabarun is a Principal Software Engineer at Broadcom, a maintainer of the Kubernetes project, an emeritus member of the Kubernetes Steering Committee member and a chair of Kubernetes SIG Contributor Experience. He is a Release Manager for Kubernetes and has been the Kubernetes 1.21 Release Team Lead. Nabarun continuously mentors newcomers in the community through various means. He has been featured multiple times in Times of India and other publications for his open source work.

name: Naoki Oguchi
bio: Naoki Oguchi is responsible for development of infrastructure software, especially developing future technologies in Linux and Kubernetes. He has been with Fujitsu since 1992, working on communication software development including Frame Relay/ATM switch, IP router, Firewall, LTE/WiMAX wireless system, WAN acceleration technique, SDN, NFV and Data center network. He has obtained a Ph.D. degree in informatics. He also co-chaired the KubeDay Japan 2022.

She is a SIG Docs Co-Chair for Kubernetes and a member of the TODO Group Steering Committee. She plays on the fun computer in her spare time. She drives VMware's cloud-native strategy, working across engineering, product, and the CNCF community to drive Kubernetes adoption, technical positioning, and developer engagement. A frequent speaker and blogger, Natalie is passionate about open source, platform engineering, and helping enterprises succeed with Kubernetes.
tagline: Principal Cloud Native Strategist & Ecosystem Lead

name: Neb Jovanovic
bio: Neb is an MLOps Engineer at Isomorphic Labs, where they build scalable ML infrastructure to accelerate AI-driven drug discovery. They currently focus on developing and refining inference graph frameworks. With a degree in biochemistry and a former career as a teacher, Neb is uniquely passionate about bridging the gap between complex biological workloads and cloud-native systems. When not wrangling YAML, they are usually playing tennis!

name: Neil Cresswell
bio:
Neil is the CEO of Portainer.io, former CEO of IndonesianCloud, former CIO of NXP New Zealand, Former VMware Consultant, and systems engineer.

bio: Niki Manoledaki is a Staff Software Engineer currently on the Platform Engineering team at Grafana Labs where she monitors carbon and cost at scale. She is a cloud sustainability advocate, keynote speaker, and community organizer. Her open source contributions include the CNCF project Kepler and Operational Resilience TAG's Green Reviews subproject. She is a CNCF Ambassador and Green Software Champion.

name: Nilekh Chaudhari

He has contributed to key upstream Kubernetes areas via SIG Auth and SIG API Machinery, the Secrets Store CSI Driver ecosystem (driver, sync controller, Azure provider), and the Gatekeeper Library. Nilekh is currently an active contributor to Istio.

role: Research Manager and Senior Technical Staff Member, IBM

bio: Nina is a software engineer working on AI Gateway inference projects. She contributes to open source projects, including Kubernetes, Istio, kagent, agentgateway, and kgateway. A CNCF Ambassador and former Kubernetes v1.33 Release Lead, she’s also a member of the Cloud Native AI Working Group and has co-authored papers on AI security. She enjoys exploring new open source projects and building AI agents—ideally so they can do her job for her. 🤖

name: Ning Liao
bio: Ning Liao is a Director of Engineering at Google, leading strategy and execution for Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) AI Platform and Distributed Compute Orchestration. Her team builds reliable, efficient, and scalable infrastructure to run the world’s largest AI/ML workloads at a massive scale, while collaborating closely with frontier AI labs. Ning brings a strong foundation in large-scale cloud infrastructure and distributed systems from previous engineering roles at AWS and Microsoft.

name: Nir Rozenbaum
bio:
Nir is an engineering leader with deep expertise in Kubernetes and Cloud-Native technologies. 
He is a Maintainer of Kubernetes Inference Gateway, Co-Chair of Kubernetes AI Gateway Working Group and a Maintainer of llm-d subprojects. 
With a proven track record in CNCF open source, he drives innovation in AI workloads on Kubernetes and helps shape industry standards for Cloud-Native inference.

name: Nont Thanonchai W
bio: Kubernetes Engineer at Northmark Compute and Cloud and an etcd contributor. Previously a senior software engineer at Microsoft and solutions architect at ExxonMobil.
