bio: Norwin Schnyder is a Cloud Software Engineer at Airlock and a Lecturer at the Eastern Switzerland University of Applied Sciences and the University of Applied Sciences and Arts Northwestern Switzerland. With over six years of experience in Kubernetes and various contributions to the Gateway API, he focuses on building secure, cloud-native ecosystems by leveraging the power of Kubernetes operators. Outside of his work, Norwin is a passionate sailor and has experience using Helm at sea.

name: Olivier Bourgeois
bio: Olivier Bourgeois is a Developer Advocate at Google. With almost 10 years of experience developing with Kubernetes, and before that with OpenStack, Olivier has a strong background in cloud and infrastructure technologies. Now, he channels this experience into advocating for the developer community, creating resources, and fostering connections to help users succeed with GKE and Kubernetes. In his spare time, Olivier enjoys spending time in nature and advocating for inclusive urbanism.

name: Omer Oz
bio: Omer is a software engineer who loves optimizing large systems. In the past he has worked across different parts of the ML Infra stack and now he works on Compute Infra at LinkedIn, helping run one of the largest Kubernetes installations in the world — +500k bare-metal machines. In his spare time, he loves testing and contributing to open source projects.

name: Omisha Gupta
bio: Hi, I'm Omisha, Solutions Architect at AWS. With a strong background in DevOps, I've been at the forefront of scaling and innovating digital solutions. My experience has empowered companies to achieve tenfold growth by leveraging AWS's cutting-edge technologies and Kubernetes. I thrive on helping businesses unlock their potential through robust, secure, and efficient cloud architectures.

name: Omri Cohen
bio: Omri Cohen is a Sr. Software Engineer at NVIDIA. He has been developing the recently open-sourced KAI scheduler and previously the Run:ai scheduler for the past 3 years.

name: Orlin Vasilev
bio: Orlin Vasilev is  Open Source and Cloud Native Technology Advocate at SAP. Community Manager for Project Harbor and Project K3s as part of the Cloud Native team. Second term CNCF Ambassador and driving the biggest Meetup Group in Bulgaria and Kubernetes Community Days Sofia organizer.. KubeCon CfP review board member and co-chair for Track 101 and Community.  Previously SysAdmin/Dev/SRE/System engineering roles for over 15 years! Located in Bulgaria, Europe! Father of two - a girl and a boy!

bio: IT Engineer with 14 years of experience, evolving from Security Architecture to Cloud and Infrastructure Engineering. Speaker at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, sharing practical insights on cloud-native technologies and platform engineering. Currently working in DevOps and transitioning into Platform Engineering, focused on automation, CI/CD, Kubernetes, containers, and Infrastructure as Code to build scalable, secure, and resilient platforms.

name: Pablo Fredrikson
bio: Principal SRE at Bitso and CNCF Ambassador. Working in the field since 2006, working with containers and Kubernetes in production since 2018. Content creator in YouTube and passionate about Open Source.

bio:
Paco is a member of Kubernetes Steering Committee, and co-chair of KubeCon+CloudNativeCon China 2024.

Paco is a kubeadm maintainer and an active kubernetes contributor. His interest includes SIG-Node, LTS and CoreDNS.

He is the leader of the open-source team in DaoCloud. He organized KCD Chengdu 2022 and KCS China 2023, and speaked in KCD Shanghai, KubeCon EU 2023 & 2024 & 2025, and KubeCon China 2021, 2023, 2024 & 2025. He is also LFAPAC Evangelist.

bio: Padma Aradhyula is a Senior Director of Software Engineering at Salesforce and a former lead for Google Dataproc’s compute fabric. Specializing in distributed systems at "planet-scale" , Padma focuses on shifting the AI and big data bottleneck from model architecture to cloud infrastructure efficiency. At Salesforce, her team manages millions of daily Spark applications on Kubernetes and working on continuous optimizations to handle the scale, reliability and price-performance of the workloads.
tagline: Solving the planet-scale infrastructure bottlenecks that data and AI leave behind.
role: Senior Director of Engineering at Salesforce

bio:
I am Parth Arora, a software developer specializing in distributed storage systems.
As a developer, I have extensive experience working with Rook, a cloud-native storage orchestrator that enables storage systems like Ceph to be run as a service on Kubernetes. I have contributed to the development of Rook and have worked on projects involving Ceph and other distributed storage systems.

name: Pavan Madduri
bio: Senior Cloud Platform Engineer at W.W. Grainger, CNCF Golden Kubestronaut, and IEEE Senior Member. I build GPU autoscaling and zero-trust infrastructure for AI workloads on Kubernetes. Creator of keda-gpu-scaler, an open-source KEDA External Scaler for GPU-aware inference scaling. Active contributor to Volcano (GPU NUMA topology) and Dragonfly (AI model distribution). I write about cloud-native AI infrastructure for CNCF.io, VKTR, and PlatformEngineering.com.
tagline: W.W.Grainger, Inc Senior Cloud Platform Engineer

bio: Pavani is a Software Development Engineer on the AWS EKS Networking team, focused on high-performance networking for AI/HPC workloads on Kubernetes. She works on EFA, RoCEv2, and RDMA integration in EKS, and contributes to the upstream DRANET project (kubernetes-sigs/dranet). Her work spans Dynamic Resource Allocation, eBPF-based network policy enforcement, and accelerator-network topology alignment for distributed training. GitHub: @Pavani-Panakanti

Peter maintains the kagent project and has been at the forefront of AI and agent projects at Solo.

name: Phelipe Fabres
bio: Phelipe Fabres is a Senior Solutions Architect specializing in Generative AI, based in São Paulo, Brazil. His focus areas include VLM fine-tuning at scale, multi-cluster GPU orchestration with CNCF projects, and cloud-native AI inference.

Expertise leading cross-functional teams, optimizing CI/CD pipelines, and enhancing/enforcing security protocols. Adept at driving and implementing technological advancements and efficient workflows to meet organizational goals and improve overall productivity.

Phill is a dedicated software engineer turned platform engineer, with a strong passion for automating processes and enabling team success. 
With extensive experience in app modernization, cloud engineering, performance tuning, and observability. Phill brings a wealth of knowledge to the table. 
Throughout their career, Phill has been committed to demystifying complex processes, making them more accessible for team members, and fostering an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive.

She champions treating infrastructure like application code, gating Flux-driven changes with in-cluster validation via Testkube, and sharing patterns teams can adopt in production.

She served on Kubernetes Release Teams from v1.23–v1.31, including as Release Lead for v1.29 (Mandala).

She is currently a Technical Lead for SIG ContribEx, a Kubernetes GitHub Admin, and was a co-chair of the first ever CNCF Maintainer Summit.

In SIG Node, she is also a core member of the "Node Readiness Controller" sub-project.

Software engineer with 20 years of experience spanning embedded Linux, systems programming, and modern C++. Former Qt maintainer and contributor to QtCore, QtMultimedia, Qt Creator, and the QNX integration layer.

bio: Rajith Attapattu is a community maintainer of OpenCost and an advocate for OpenTelemetry and open standards. His current focus is intent-based observability, AIOps, and building intelligent, cost-efficient telemetry pipelines. He previously spent over a decade at Red Hat working on distributed systems.

name: Randi Armour
bio: Randi Armour has spent four years at the Linux Foundation, starting with supporting the growth of open source projects including OpenSSF, Yocto Project, AGL, and CIP. Now an Account Manager in LF Education, she helps private sector, government, and public sector organizations worldwide build skills in cloud native, Linux and embedded systems, AI/ML, and cybersecurity, drawing on firsthand experience across multiple open source communities.

bio: Rani Chowdary Mandepudi is an Arm engineer and open source contributor focused on enabling cloud native workloads on Arm. Rani contributed the upstream Harbor arm64 enablement work, including build/package workflow changes and follow-up dependency fixes, and works with CNCF communities to make Arm support part of normal project release paths.

Rashmi is a Senior Software Engineer at Red Hat and a maintainer of the Operator Framework. She has worked across Operator SDK and Operator Lifecycle Manager, helping shape the technologies that enable Kubernetes operators to be built, distributed, and managed at scale.

She focuses on the next generation of Operator Lifecycle Management, building scalable APIs and controllers for Kubernetes extensions. She is passionate about open source, distributed systems, and cloud-native technologies.

name: Ratnopam Chakrabarti
bio: Ratnopam Chakrabarti is a Senior Solutions Architect in AWS's AI/ML organization specializing in AI infrastructure on Kubernetes—spanning AI inference, model fine-tuning, building MLOps pipelines, and running agentic AI systems in production. An active adopter and contributor to CNCF projects, he has previously spoken at events like KCD Texas, Ray Summit and advocates for open-source approaches to running AI infrastructure and agents on Kubernetes.

He is an author of a book focused applied generative modeling, Bayesian Modeling and Computation in Python.

In her free time, she loves training jiu-jitsu, landscaping & gardening, and watching horror movies.

He's passionate about making distributed systems work in environments that are anything but predictable — where the "nodes" walk, fall, and get back up. Outside of work, he geeks out on cloud networking, robot identity, and whatever edge case the robots throw at him next.

Ricardo is a Cloud Native AI Lead. He's an open-source enthusiast, currently serving on the CNCF TOC. He has also co-chaired the CNCF TAG-Runtime. Recently, he led the publication of the Cloud Native AI Whitepaper and is currently helping with various initiatives within the Cloud Native AI and PyTorch ecosystem, including the PyTorch Technical Advisory Council (TAC).

He has a diverse professional background spanning over 25 years in tech and software engineering at both large companies.

He has led for several years the internal effort to transition services and workloads to use cloud native technologies, as well as dissemination and training efforts. name: Robin Deaconu

name: Roger Coll

He thrives on building internal developer platforms using open-source technologies to increase development velocity. Outside of work, you may find him backpacking around the world, always seeking his next adventure.

name: Alolita Sharma
bio: Alolita Sharma is a OpenTelemetry maintainer and GC member. Also she is a CNCF End-User TAB & GB member. She leads Apple’s AIML observability teams. She contributes to open source, open standards at OpenTelemetry, Unicode, W3C. She has been co-chair of CNCF's Observability TAG and has served on the boards of the OSI, SFLC.in and Unicode Consortium. Previously Alolita led observability and search engineering teams at AWS and has managed engineering teams at IBM, PayPal, Twitter, Wikipedia.

role: OpenTelemetry GC Member & Maintainer, Observability Engineering Leader at Apple

name: Aman Singh
bio:
Principal Software Engineer in the office of Microsoft Azure's CTO and maintainer of Drasi. Organizer of the CNCF community group for Seattle.

Speaker @ KubeCon NA 2025 and program committee member for KubeCon India 2026 and KubeCon Japan 2026, Aman also mentors students through GSoC and LFX on projects spanning agentic AI, MCP & IoT.

Aman has 12+ years of distributed systems experience at LinkedIn and Microsoft - spanning stream processing, and building new Azure services from the ground up.
tagline: Principal Software Engineer at office of Microsoft Azure CTO
role: Engineering Leader at Microsoft Azure CTO's Office · Drasi Maintainer · CNCF organizer

name: Ana Marques
bio: Ana is a graphic designer at Avalia Systems, where she works with engineers to turn complex technical concepts into something people can actually grasp. Lately she has been using AI tools to stretch her creativity beyond visuals and into working code.

name: André Wanlin
bio: André, a full Stack Developer from Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada, is a Core Maintainer, Community Plugin Maintainer and Documentation Maintainer of the Backstage open source project having contributed 3 plugins - Azure DevOps, DevTools, and Linguist - as well as various features, bug fixes and documentation updates. He's also an active CNCF Ambassador where he shares his Backstage knowledge with other CNCF projects and co-chairs BackstageCon which takes place as part of KubeCon. He's often found on the Backstage Discord Server helping others and sharing his passion for all things Backstage. When he's offline you can catch him at the local dog park with his Frenchton Bailey!

name: Andrew Chin
bio:
Andrew is part of Team Atlanta, the winning team in the AIxCC finals competition at DEF CON 33.

He is currently a Ph.D. student at the Georgia Institute of Technology, working with Prof. Taesoo Kim at the Systems Software & Security Lab. Building on the work from AIxCC, Andrew is leading a Team Atlanta effort — in partnership with the OpenSSF — to strengthen the security of open source software through OSS-CRS, a unified framework and standard for the next generation of Cyber Reasoning Systems.
tagline: Georgia Institute of Technology, PhD Student

name: Andrew Martin
bio: Andrew has an incisive security engineering ethos gained building and destroying high-traffic web applications. Proficient in systems development, testing, and operations, he is at his happiest profiling and securing every tier of a cloud native system, and has battle-hardened experience delivering containerised solutions to enterprise and government. He is CEO at https://control-plane.io

name: Andy Zhang
bio: Andy Zhang is a Principal Software Engineer at Microsoft, leading storage and AI infrastructure in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). Currently focusing on building AI/LLM inference infrastructure on Kubernetes. Maintainer of multiple CNCF projects including KAITO, NFS/SMB CSI drivers and Azure CSI drivers (Disk, File, Blob).

name: Anthony Burris
bio:
Anthony Burris is a Director of Cloud and Infrastructure Engineering at Morgan Stanley, where he leads cloud infrastructure initiatives with a focus on GitOps and platform engineering. He is a key contributor to Morgan Stanley’s FluxCD adoption and integration, helping drive GitOps practices at enterprise scale.
Outside of technology, Anthony is a father of three who enjoys tackling home improvement projects, following NFL football [ Go Birds], and generally finding new things to build.
tagline: Director, Cloud & Infra Engineering III, Morgan Stanley

name: Antoine Toulme
bio: I work at Splunk where I serve the team working on the OpenTelemetry Collector. I am a contributor to the OpenTelemetry Collector. I am or have been active on the Eclipse project, the Apache Software Foundation and the Hyperledger Foundation. I hail from San Jose, California!
tagline: Leave it better than you found it

name: Antonio Jimenez Martinez
bio:
I am a Tech Lead Software Engineer at Cisco ThousandEyes, specializing in observability to ensure our customers can effectively monitor their products. My recent work involves using OpenTelemetry to stream telemetry data, enhancing network visibility and performance for our clients.


I actively participate in the tech community, frequently attending conferences and meet-ups to share knowledge and stay abreast of industry trends.
tagline: Cisco ThousandEyes, Tech Lead Software Engineer

name: Anubhab Majumdar
bio: I’m a Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft working on Kubernetes networking, observability, and security in both Azure and open-source projects including Cilium and Retina. My work centers on improving how cloud native systems are monitored, secured, debugged, and operated at scale.

name: Arpit Jain
bio: Supply-chain security researcher focused on CI/CD pipeline vulnerabilities. Audits GitHub Actions workflows across CNCF, sigstore/SLSA, OpenSSF, and US federal government orgs (cisagov, GSA) for exploitable patterns: pwn requests, unpinned actions, token-scope misconfigurations. Has privately disclosed CVE-class vulnerabilities including a CRITICAL pwn-request finding in Apache Doris. Builds open-source scanners for mitigation-aware CI/CD vulnerability detection.

name: Artem Lajko
bio:
Artem Lajko, certified CNCF Kubestronaut, specializes in Kubernetes scalability and GitOps-driven workflows. He is the author of Implementing GitOps with Kubernetes and writing for various publishers.

As a Platform Engineering Ambassador, he supports companies and the community in adopting Platform Engineering. Passionate about Open Source, he helps organizations choose the right tools, driving tech adoption and innovation.
tagline: Head of Platform Engineering at iits-consulting

name: Artur Ciocanu
bio: Artur Ciocanu has worn many hats: C#, Flash/Flex, and JavaScript developer, and for the last decade mostly a builder of distributed systems in Java, Spring Boot, and the major cloud platforms. As an architect and team lead he got pulled into cloud-agnostic tech like Dapr, the CNCF project, where he contributes Spring Boot support to the Dapr Java SDK. Lately he works on the unglamorous infrastructure behind AI agents: supply chain for agent skills, and agent memory as a stateful data problem.
tagline: Lead Senior Computer Scientist at Adobe

name: Atulpriya Sharma
bio:
Known across the cloud-native community as Maharaj, I make complex technology accessible - from KubeCon stages to community meetups to client boardrooms. What started as a manual QA engineering career over a decade ago has evolved into leading developer relations at scale as a Principal Developer Advocate. 

Speaker at every KubeCon since Chicago 2023, Co-Chair of KubeCon India 2025, Co-Chair of the CNCF Platform Engineering Technical Community Group, and organiser of Cloud Native Hyderabad.
tagline: Principal Developer Advocate @ Improving | CNCF Ambassador

name: Austin Parker
bio: Austin is a founding member of the OpenTelemetry project, long-time developer advocate and speaker, and currently a member of the OpenTelemetry Governance Committee. He works at honeycomb.io leading AI strategy and helping advance the state of the art in observability for modern systems.

name: Bailey Hayes
bio: Bailey Hayes is the CTO at Cosmonic and has applied Wasm experience across diverse domains, including building graphics-intensive web applications, User-Defined Functions (UDFs) in databases, IoT solutions, and cloud-native microservices powered by wasmCloud. She wears many hats in the open source ecosystem from standards to implementations as the W3C WebAssembly WASI Subgroup co-chair, Bytecode Alliance TSC Director, and maintainer of CNCF wasmCloud.
tagline: CTO at Cosmonic | TSC Director at Bytecode Alliance | W3C WebAssembly WASI Subgroup Co-Chair

name: Balaji Sivasubramanian
bio:
Balaji Sivasubramanian is the Head of Product, Developer Experience at Red Hat, where he leads a portfolio of developer-focused products including Red Hat Developer Hub (enterprise-grade Backstage distribution), Podman Desktop (with AI Lab for local model experimentation), and DevSpaces (cloud IDE). His work centers on advancing AI-powered developer productivity, platform engineering, and cloud-native workflows for enterprise developers.

Previously, Balaji was EVP of Product at OpsMx, driving innovations in intelligent and secure multi-cloud application delivery. Earlier in his career, he held senior product leadership roles at Cisco, focusing on cloud-native solutions. With over 20 years of experience in developer tools, DevOps, and AI platforms, he has also been an active leader in open source communities including Backstage, Kubernetes, Argo CD, and Spinnaker.
tagline: Head of Developer Experience,  Red Hat

name: Baruch Sadogursky
bio:
Baruch Sadogursky (@jbaruch) did Java before it had generics, DevOps before there was Docker, and DevRel before it had a name. He built DevRel at JFrog from a ten-person company through an IPO, co-authored "Liquid Software" and "DevOps Tools for Java Developers," and is a Java Champion, a Microsoft MVP for AI, and a CNCF Ambassador alum.

Today he's head of DevRel at Port, working on the agentic SDLC, and a self-certified Level 3 AI Context Sommelier.

name: Bert Bullough
bio: Bert Bullough is Lead Architect for Research Cloud Computing at Idaho National Laboratory, where he heads INL's Salt Lake City office at the University of Utah and is standing up GPU infrastructure for agentic AI inside a FedRAMP High / IL5 boundary under the DOE Genesis Mission. A two-time AWS Solutions Architect – Professional with 20 years in industry, he leads the DevSecOps practice for research computing and works at the seam where agentic systems meet federal change-control and compliance.
tagline: Lead Architect, Research Cloud Computing — Idaho National Laboratory (Salt Lake City)

name: Bjorn Hovland
bio: Bjorn Hovland is President of CIQ, which leads sovereign AI initiatives for governments, universities, and research organizations with stacks underpinned by open source   infrastructure components including Rocky Linux.

name: Boteng Yao
bio: Boteng Yao is a Senior Software Engineer at Google, Senior Envoy Maintainer. He specializes in data plane architecture, security, reliability, and AI networking, contributing to both Envoy open source and Google’s production platforms

name: Bradley Andersen
bio: Mentor | Community Builder | Kubestronaut | B2 German | I unify + grow people + processes.

name: Carl Ross
bio: Member of Technical Staff @ OpenAI

bio: Carl-Fredrik Sundström is a Senior Principal Cloud Native Software Architect at Ericsson, bringing 30 years of experience in telecommunications and IT. Having held technical and leadership roles across the globe, he now focuses on cloud-native architecture, Kubernetes, GitOps, and software delivery automation. He is passionate about bridging enterprise-scale software engineering with open-source technologies to simplify the deployment and lifecycle management of complex systems.
role: Senior Principal Developer, cloud native architecture

name: Carlos Sanchez
bio: Carlos Sanchez is a Principal Scientist at Adobe Experience Manager, specializing in software automation an agentic applications. Involved in Open Source for over 20 years, he is the author of the Jenkins Kubernetes plugin and a member of the Apache Software Foundation amongst other open source groups, contributing to several projects, such as Kubernetes, Jenkins or Apache Maven.

name: Cecil Wöbker
bio: Cecil Wöbker is Co-Founder & CTO at remberg, a Munich-based company building an AI-first platform for industrial asset management. He studied Computer Science at TU Munich and Technology Management at CDTM. Cecil leads remberg's technological development, helping industrial companies digitize maintenance and service processes through cloud-based solutions and AI copilots.

name: Chad M. Crowell
bio: Chad is a CNCF Ambassador and Principal SRE at Akamai. Chad is the author of the book "Acing the Certified Kubernetes Administrator Exam." Chad also enjoys teaching Kubernetes in the small community-led group KubeSkills.
tagline: Principal SRE at Akamai, CNCF Ambassador, Speaker, and Author

tagline: Software Engineer II @ Circles | CNCF Ambassador | GDG Organizer

name: Chandra Siva
bio: Chandra Siva is a Sr. Distinguished Engineer at Capital One, focused on observability and reliability platforms, with 30+ years building distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and developer platforms. Previously led technical efforts at GM/Cruise (distributed tracing across cloud, data center, connected-vehicle systems) and Exabeam (cloud-native, Kubernetes-based security platform across multiple regions). Passionate about resilient systems and simplifying infrastructure for engineers.

name: Cheslav Versky
bio: Cheslav Versky focuses on driving developer velocity by helping organizations build, scale, and optimize the adoption of CNCF-compliant Kubernetes and modern application architectures for large enterprises across the AMER region; he holds the title of Principal Architect.

name: Chetan Sharma
bio: Chetan Sharma is a software engineer specializing in large-scale data storage, processing, and ingestion systems. His career has included roles at Google, Microsoft, and IBM Research, where he has focused on solving complex challenges in distributed systems. He earned his master's degree in Computer Science from Pennsylvania State University with an emphasis on distributed systems.

Helping to connect the Software Development Community in the

PHP Argentina

bio: Chris Plank is an Enterprise Architect, Product Owner and Platform as a Product evangelist at NatWest Bank in Scotland. He has been leading a Platform as a Product initiative within the Bank since 2023 working on radically changing the Banks approach to provisioning and maintaining services. Outside of work, Chris contributes to the Open Source Community as one of the CNCF Platform Engineering Technical Community Group Leaders as well as being an OpenUK Ambassador.
role: Enterprise Architect, Platform Engineering Evangelist, Product Owner

name: Christian Hernandez
bio: Christian is a well rounded technologist with experience in infrastructure engineering, systems administration, enterprise architecture, tech support, advocacy, and product management. Passionate about OpenSource and containerizing the world one application at a time. He is currently a maintainer of the Argo Project and OpenGitops. Currently, he works as a Technical Marketing Engineer and Tech Lead at Cisco. He focuses on GitOps practices, DevOps, Kubernetes, Network Security, and Containers.

name: Christian Mesh
bio: Christian is a Maintainer of OpenTofu and serves on it's Technical Steering Committee .  He is generously sponsored by Spacelift.

name: Christophe Sauthier
bio:
Christophe directs CNCF's training and certification programs.
He defines CNCF's vision for courses and certifications, and follows every step of its realization.
Christophe is an Open Source veteran with over 20 years' experience both in the community (Ubuntu, OpenStack, Cloud Native...) and in professional services.
Living in Montreal but originally from France, he enjoys spending time with his wife and children when he's not on the basketball court, his other great passion.

name: Cijo Thomas
bio: Cijo is a Software Engineer at Apple working on Observability. Previously, he worked on observability and telemetry solutions at Microsoft. He has been involved with OpenTelemetry since its inception and is a core maintainer of the OpenTelemetry .NET and Rust implementations. He is also an Approver for the OpenTelemetry Specification and OpenTelemetry Arrow projects.

name: Colin Griffin
bio:
Colin Griffin is CEO at Krumware, and a Co-Chair of the CNCF Platforms Working Group. Colin Griffin is a software engineer by trade, specializing in cloud-native application and infrastructure development; with an emphasis on developer enablement and platform engineering. He founded Krumware with the goal of enabling companies to build better environments for their developers, through technology development.
Krumware helps organizations build better software.

name: Colin O'Dell
bio: Colin O'Dell is a Lead Software Engineer on SeatGeek's Platform team, where he accelerates business outcomes by increasing software teams’ efficiency, effectiveness, and empowerment.

name: Corey McGalliard
bio: My team and I power and protect life online by building an internal, opinionated Kubernetes platform that meets Akamai's change-safety, security, and compliance expectations while delivering an excellent developer experience. I have had the opportunity to contribute to the CNCF Platforms Community Group Initiatives, updating the Platform Maturity Model and Whitepaper. I believe that computing systems allow me to love my neighbors well by providing excellence in the Cloud Native industry.

name: Craig Sebenik
bio:
Recovering sysadmin and SRE.
Observability is the core of healthy software.

Currently, a cloud engineer working on self-driving vehicles.

name: Damien O'Toole
bio:
Highly experienced engineer with over two decades of professional experience in software design. Since joining Ericsson in 2000, Damien has worked through many transformations in software development practices. contributing significantly to various projects and initiatives. 

More recently, Damien in his role as a Developer Advocate and as part of the DX team, plays a central role in both defining the architecture of Ericsson's IDP & driving the implementation of the broader DX initiative.

name: Dan Garfield
bio:
Dan Garfield is the Co-founder and Chief Open Source Officer of Codefresh, a CI/CD platform powered by GitOps and Argo. As an Argo Maintainer, he works parmiarily on Argo CD and Argo Rollouts. He helped create the GitOps Working Group and Open GitOps Principles. He helped create the most popular GitOps certification with Argo CD and writes consistently about best practices for GitOps involving Security, Development processes, and scaling.

Catch him in the Argo documentary!
tagline: Argo Maintainer, Open GitOps Co-Creator, Codefresh Founder

name: Danilo Souza
bio: Senior DevOps Architect at Amazon specializing in cloud-native infrastructure and Kubernetes implementations at scale. With 10+ years of experience and an MSc in Computer Science, I architect solutions bridging AI/ML systems with container orchestration. A certified Kubernetes Kubestronaut, passionate about standardizing communication between LLMs and infrastructure resources.

name: David Aronchick
bio:
I am CEO and co-founder of Expanso, the company behind the distributed compute platform Bacalhau. This means I spend most of my time helping humans to convince machines to be smarter. I am only moderately successful at this.

Previously, I led product management for Kubernetes on behalf of Google, launched GKE, and co-founded the Kubeflow project, and led Open Source ML Strategy at Azure. I have also worked at Protocol Labs, Amazon and Chef and co-founded three startups.

name: David Pech
bio: Accomplished DevOps professional with 20 years of experience in software development and infrastructure management. Proficient in a wide array of technologies within the Kubernetes and CNCF ecosystem, with a focus on producing high-quality, sustainable software solutions. Known for a pragmatic and security-conscious approach to technology adoption. Passionate about educating and enabling teams in the adoption and understanding of cloud technologies.
tagline: Kubernetes, ArgoCD, AWS, OCI, Postgres fan

bio: Derek Wang is a Principal Software Engineer working for Intuit, his main focus is on the architecture of streaming data processing platforms as well as event-driven systems. He is the project lead of a couple of open source projects: CNCF graduated project Argo Events, and Numaflow.

name: Diana Todea
bio: Diana is a CNCF Ambassador and an OpenTelemetry Docs Approver. She organizes Cloud Native Days Romania, is a CNCF Operational Resilience TAG Lead and supports underrepresented groups in tech.

name: Dipanwita Guhathakurta
bio: Dipanwita Guhathakurta is a Software Engineer at the IBM T.J.Watson Research Center in New York. Her interests lie in AI platform optimization, hybrid cloud research, inference performance estimation and modeling.

name: Dotan Horovits
bio:
Horovits is an international speaker and thought leader, as well as a CNCF and OpenSearch Ambassador. His passion domain is observability, and has been hosting the popular OpenObservability Talks podcast for seven years.

Horovits works as a senior open source advocate at Amazon Web Services, with special focus on the OpenSearch project, open observability, and open source practices.
tagline: Sr. Open Source Advocate; CNCF & OpenSearch Ambassador
role: Sr. Open Source Advocate; CNCF & OpenSearch Ambassador

bio:
Develops FOSS tools and methods to effectively defend critical infrastructure using modern tech. Builds algorithms for sovereignty, understanding and long term sustainability.

Constanze is a physicist (Albert Einstein Institute and Johns Hopkins) and left academia for a decade leading digital transformation initiatives in regulated sectors. Now, funds her research independently and partners with universities and research institutes. Founded fusioncore.ai and CNCG "Securitynative Europe"

name: Eduardo Silva
bio: Eduardo is an entrepreneur and Software Engineer. He is one of Fluentd project maintainers and creator of Fluent Bit, a lightweight Logs, Metrics, and Traces processor.

name: Ekansh Gupta
bio: Ekansh is a Software Development Engineer, with active involvement in various open-source and cloud native communities for upwards two years now. He was previously an SDE Intern at SteamLabs. He is also a speaker for a couple of talks at PyCon, KubeCon and MozFests. Ekansh is a Google Summer of Code mentor too where he mentored for Circuitverse in 2021. He loves to write blogs and communicate with people that can help the community thrive.

name: Emily Chen
bio:
Emily is a solutions engineer at Akuity, an Argo enthusiast, and a CNCF Ambassador. She is an active contributor to various CNCF projects, including translation efforts for ebpf.io and the CNCF Glossary, and an advocate for diversity and inclusion.

Outside of CNCF, Emily is a contributor to the scikit-learn Machine Learning & Data Science library, a life-long language learner, and a bookworm.

name: Erica Hughberg
bio:
Erica Hughberg is a technical leader, experienced public speaker, and community advocate passionate about helping engineering teams build scalable, secure, and human-centric platforms for the AI era.

As a maintainer of Envoy AI Gateway, she plays a key role in enabling organizations to securely and efficiently integrate AI-powered services into their systems and solutions.

name: Erika Alvarez
bio: Erika Alvarez is a DevOps engineer at Qualabs, specializing in video and streaming media infrastructure. Based in Montevideo, Uruguay, she works at the intersection of traditional DevOps practices and the operational demands of live and on-demand video platforms. She holds AWS certifications and has hands-on experience building cloud-native infrastructure for streaming workflows using Kubernetes, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, FFmpeg, and TSDuck.

name: Evaline Ju
bio: Evaline is a senior engineer working on the AI platform engineering team of IBM Research and based in Denver, Colorado. Her work focuses on platform-level concerns for agent workloads including guardrails and observability. She is also a contributor to the Kubernetes agentic networking group.
tagline: Senior Software Engineer at IBM Research

name: Evan Shortiss
bio: Evan Shortiss is a Technical Marketing Manager at Red Hat. He helps customers and field teams succeed with cloud-native technologies, maintains demo and workshop infrastructure, and creates technical enablement content. He's focused on cloud-native technologies, building mobile and web applications, and services using JavaScript ecosystem technologies.
tagline: Technical Marketing Manager at Red Hat

name: Fabian Kammel
bio: Fabian Kammel is a Senior Security Consultant at ControlPlane, where he helps to make the (cloud-native) world a safer place. His goal is to bring hardware security and cloud-native security closer together, as well as, improving the developer experience in the security space. He previously spoke at KubeCon, SigstoreCon, was a guest on the Kubernetes Podcast, and regular host of the CNCF TAG Security.

name: Fabrizio Lazzaretti
bio: Fabrizio Lazzaretti is a Senior Managing Consultant at Wavestone and CNCF Ambassador, bridging cloud-native technology with enterprise architecture. A CloudEvents maintainer and co-author of Crafting Great APIs with Domain-Driven Design, he has deep expertise in event-driven architecture, microservices, and AI products. With 10+ years across software architecture, development, and DevOps, he leads cross-industry engagements that align technology with business goals and close the business-IT gap.

Since then, I've dived headfirst into the world of information technology, enjoying the constant evolution of systems and technologies, programming languages, being an insatiable learner and a high-level engineer. Scalability and flexibility are my passions. My job is my favorite game.

name: Faseela Kundattil

She has given talks and workshops at several conferences evangelizing CNCF projects, including the recent KubeCons. She is a CNCF Ambassador, LFX Mentor, and the winner of the prestigious CNCF “Chop Wood Carry Water” award, 2023. She is also the creator of "Izzy saves the Birthday", a children's illustrated book from Istio.

He has spent 40+ years in software, with a common thread of communications and security throughout, and is a coauthor of Linkerd: Up and Running from O'Reilly, a co-lead of the AI Gateway Working Group and Gateway API for service mesh, and the original author of the Emissary-ingress API gateway. He is most easily found as @flynn on the CNCF or Linkerd Slacks.

name: Francesco Beltramini
bio: Francesco is a Security Professional with 15+ years of working experience and deep technical competence matured on a number of high-end projects for both public and private sector organisations. Francesco had the opportunity of working on a variety of technology stacks in designing and implementing complex security architectures in both the IT and OT spaces, from Cloud to mission-critical/safety-critical/high-assurance infrastructure.

name: Gang Luo

His focus is on building scalable platforms, enabling developer productivity, and driving operational excellence within fast-growing organizations.

He maintains Projectsveltos — Kubernetes controllers that simplify add-on and application management across fleets of clusters — and k8s-cleaner, which automatically removes unused or unhealthy cluster resources. Outside work, he spends time with his family and manages two fantasy soccer leagues.

His educational background shapes his view of technology as a storytelling medium using data and cloud. At North America's largest bank by market cap, Gonzalo advocates for open source and data democratization.

As a core contributor and reviewer in the Kubernetes community, Grant has delivered talks at KubeCon, GopherCon, and HashiTalks on topics ranging from CSI drivers to resilient data pipelines.

He brings expertise in Kubernetes, Red Hat OpenShift, and cloud‑native platforms and architectures, enabling organizations to build scalable, high-performance systems.

bio:
I help platform engineers and DevOps teams understand and adopt cloud-native infrastructure through talks, demos, and community building. bio: Vadim Bauer is a Container Silverback with over a decade of experience in running containers in production. As a maintainer of the CNCF project Harbor, he focuses on extending the boundaries of OCI artifact management, adoption, and developer experience. At 8gears, Vadim helps cloud providers, ISVs and enterprises adopt Harbor and use OCI capabilities.
tagline: Cloud Native builder in the Clouds with Kubernetes. CNCF Project Harbor maintainer.

name: Valentina Rodriguez Sosa
bio:
I've more than 18 years of experience defining and implementing software architectures by leading
high-performance teams and improving best practices for software development. I help connect people
with technology by bringing value to their businesses. Passionate about cloud computing, Kubernetes, AI,
and distributed systems. I have presented as a speaker at several events, including KubeCon, KCD NY, OSS, and others.
I am Project Maintainer for Kubeflow.
tagline: Principal AI Architect FSI | Safety & Security

name: Vamsi Kalapala
bio: Vamsi is a Software Engineer at Palantir. Previously at Microsoft working on Azure container networking team.

name: Venkat Gattupalli
bio: Venkat Gattupalli is a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI, where he enables frontier-scale AI infrastructure for pre-training. His work brings high-performance networking into cloud-native environments while preserving workload isolation, reliability, and operational simplicity. Before OpenAI, he was a Traffic Engineering Lead at eBay, helping lead its move to cloud-native service mesh, software-defined load balancing, and resilient traffic orchestration across hundreds of Kubernetes clusters.
tagline: Scaling Infrastructure for Frontier Models @ OpenAI

name: Vicente Herrera
bio: Principal Consultant at Control Plane, focusing on Kubernetes and AI cybersecurity for fintech organizations. Co-author of FINOS AI Governance Framework. Lecturer at Loyola University in Seville for the Master's program in Artificial Intelligence, on AI security and AI Ethics. Author of "Building intelligent cloud applications" published by O'Reilly about Azure ML services. Regular speaker at international conferences.

name: Vijay Samuel
bio: Vijay Samuel works with eBay's observability platform as its architect. During his time at eBay Vijay has transformed eBay's observability platform into a cloud native offering that is primarily built on top of open source technologies. He loves to code in Go and play video games.

name: Vinay Gonuguntla
bio: Vinay is a Sr Staff Software Engineer at Intuit. Currently working in the Service Mesh team and also working on migrating and moving micro-services into service mesh. He enjoys dev-ops and automating tasks.

name: Vincent Caldeira
bio: Vincent Caldeira, Red Hat APAC CTO and Industry Visiting Scholar at Columbia University, drives tech strategy and emerging engineering. A Top 10 APAC CTO (2023) with 20+ years in finance IT, he is an authority on open source, cloud-native technologies and AI. Vincent holds leadership roles across the Linux Foundation (FINOS, LF AI & Data) and GSF, championing AI safety, sustainability, and digital sovereignty.
tagline: Leading Open Source Technology Innovation for a Sustainable Future

name: William Rizzo
bio:
William is a CNCF Ambassador and Linkerd Ambassador currently working at Mirantis as Global Field CTO. He’s focused on helping customers designing, building, and running their initiatives on Edge, AI and Platform Engineering. He wore many hats in the IT world, Engineering, Pre-Post sales, Product Owner and Consulting. from HPC, Storage to Distributed Systems.
William enjoys volunteering in several Cloud Native groups and organizing the KCD Netherlands events.

name: Yan Avlasov
bio: Yan Avlasov is a senior maintainer of Envoy proxy. Yan works at Google, helping teams deploy Envoy based products and ensuring that Envoy and Envoy based products meet Google’s standards for safety and security.

name: Yuan Tang
bio: Co-founder at TensorScale AI, focusing on building AI stack for world models. He led AI infrastructure and platform teams at various companies, including Red Hat and Alibaba. He holds leadership roles in open source communities — including Argo, Kubeflow, KServe, Kubernetes, and CNCF — and maintains many open source projects. Yuan has authored award-winning books and highly cited papers and patents, and is a frequent keynote speaker, technical advisor, and mentor at various organizations.

name: Yuchen Fama
bio: Yuchen is currently a builder, benchmarker, and inference product manager at Red Hat AI. She has more than 15 years of experience in ML and AI, has served as VP of Product, CTO, and CPO at multiple AI startups, and has led AI/ML research teams within several Fortune 500 companies. She has a Ph.D. in Statistics.
tagline: Senior Principal Product Manager, Inference, Red Hat

name: Yuriy Natarov
bio: Yuriy is Inference Provisioning Team Lead for Nebius Token Factory, where he works on Kubernetes-based infrastructure for large-scale LLM inference. As one of the first backend engineers on the project, he helped scale the platform and team by more than 10x in under a year.
tagline: Inference Provisioning Team Lead @ Nebius Token Factory

name: Zach Aller
bio: Zach Aller is a software engineer at Intuit and a lead maintainer of Argo Rollouts. He has 15+ years of software development experience with a strong focus on SRE/Platform tooling. He has a strong background in Kubernetes and has managed large scale Kubernetes clusters for multiple organizations. He is is a strong proponent in GitOps style deployments which he has implemented at scale.

name: Zameer Fouzan
bio:
Zameer Fouzan is a Lead Developer Relations Engineer with a background in full-stack and cloud engineering, focused on observability, OpenTelemetry, and cloud-native systems. 

In his current role at New Relic, Zameer leads DevRel initiatives across the APJ region, delivering technical talks, hands-on workshops, and community programs. He is known for system-level, implementable sessions that help developers make complex systems more visible, reliable, and operable at scale.

name: Zihan Zheng
bio: Zihan Zheng is a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI, where he works on large-scale inference systems for frontier models. His research focuses on AI evaluation, coding agents, and benchmark design. He led LiveCodeBench Pro and has authored work published at NeurIPS, ICLR, and ICML. He received his B.S. in Computer Science from NYU.
